docs.title: Rupee jumps 177 paise in 2 days against dollar after RBI's strong defence before Rs 97 goal post. What lie
docs.text:
The rupee has recorded a stellar comeback, strengthening nearly 177 paise against the US dollar in just two sessions after the RBI announced several measures to protect the falling Indian currency, although analysts highlight that the gains may be temporary amid strong macro headwinds.
 The rupee jumped 82 paise on Tuesday to 94.06 against the US dollar in early trade on Tuesday. Overall, the Indian currency has gained around Rs 1.77 against the US dollar in two sessions from Friday's closing level of 96.73.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Saturday announced four measures, including a dedicated dollar supply window for three state-run oil companies, tighter restrictions on foreign exchange derivatives, a 20% cash reserve requirement for certain currency contracts and stricter daily cash reserve requirements for banks.
 Also read | Rupee stages stunning comeback against dollar: What’s the RBI’s 4-step shock therapy and how long can it last? 
Later on Monday, RBI tightened rules on rupee non-deliverable derivative contracts, limiting overseas clients to using them only for hedging, and widened a 20% cash reserve requirement to banks' own rupee currency hedges.
 Live Events
 What lies ahead for rupee? 
RBI's latest moves are expected to reduce pressure on the spot market and curb speculative dollar buying, supporting the currency in the near term, said Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst of Commodity and Currency at LKP Securities . "With the RBI's measures supporting the rupee, we expect USD/INR to move towards 95.00-94.80 range in the near term," PTI quoted CR Forex Advisors MD Amit Pabari as saying.
The announcements made by the RBI over the weekend clearly reflect its intent to drain excess liquidity from the system, while the timing may be read by the market as a tolerance level for Rs 97 that the regulator intends to defend, JM Financial said. It now expects the rupee to appreciate to 94-94.5 per US dollar in the near term before heading towards 97-97.5. "But we see upside risk to our earlier expectations of 7.5% levels on domestic yields."
Trivedi from LKP Securities however warned that a sustained recovery will depend on FII flows, crude oil prices and broader dollar movement. This comes as FIIs continue to remain bearish on Indian markets, heavily selling Indian equities while oil prices and bond yields continue to soar and spook investors.
 Also read | RBI tightens rules on rupee non-deliverable contracts, widens 20% cash reserve requirement 
"If these exogenous factors persist for long, exerting pressure on the capital account, the government should start evaluating fiscal measures to attract FII flows," JM Financial said, adding that if crude price spikes incrementally or even remain at current levels for long, then all emerging market currencies including the rupee could come under pressure.
Although these steps will be effective in draining excess liquidity, JM Financial said that the impact on the rupee seems temporary as they are not effective on macro challenges such as elevated crude oil and FII selling.
 Also read | Why is the market rising today?

docs.title: NTPC in talks with Japan, South Korea, Germany for green fuel exports
docs.text:
New Delhi: India 's top power producer NTPC is in talks with potential buyers in Japan, South Korea and Germany for green ammonia and other low-carbon fuels , Chairman Gurdeep Singh said on Tuesday.
 India has outlined plans to become a major green hydrogen producer, even as developers worldwide have struggled to secure the long-term offtake agreements required to underpin large-scale investments
 Also Read: NTPC to set aside Rs 16,70,000 crore for capex over next 11 years; focuses on nuclear power, renewables and battery storage, eyes 250 GW capacity by 2037 
NTPC is in talks with prospective overseas customers as it develops a proposed green hydrogen hub in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh, Singh said at an event organised by the Indian Chamber of Commerce
The project is expected to produce green ammonia and green methanol , which are considered more practical than hydrogen for transportation and international trade 
 Live Events
"We have to make hydrogen a business," Singh said, adding that the focus was shifting from pilot projects to commercially viable ventures
 Also Read: NTPC may buy 10 million tonnes of coal from commercial mines 
The comments underscore efforts by Indian companies to secure demand as they seek to turn government-backed hydrogen ambitions into commercially viable projects
Backed by subsidies of roughly $2.1 billion, New Delhi aims to produce 5 million metric tons of green hydrogen annually by 2030
Demand for green ⁠fuels is expected to rise as industries look for alternatives to fossil fuels to reduce missions and ⁠meet decarbonisation targets

docs.title: Vaibhav Vyapaar IPO opens for subscription today: Check price band and other key details
docs.text:
The initial public offering of Vaibhav Vyapaar opens for subscription on Tuesday, on the NSE SME platform. The issue will remain open for bidding for three days, closing on October 15, 2026.
 Vaibhav Vyapaar IPO is a book-built issue worth Rs 42.10 crore, comprising an entirely fresh issue of 77.96 lakh shares. The allotment is expected to be finalised on October 16, while the company’s shares are tentatively scheduled to list on the NSE SME platform on October 21, 2026.
The company has fixed the price band for its IPO at Rs 51–54 per share. The minimum application lot comprises 2,000 shares. At the upper end of the price band, retail investors must apply for at least 4,000 shares, requiring a minimum investment of Rs 2,16,000.
For high-net-worth individual (HNI) investors, the minimum application size is three lots, or 6,000 shares, amounting to Rs 3,24,000 at the upper price band.
GetFive Advisors Pvt. Ltd. is the book-running lead manager for the issue, while KFin Technologies Ltd. is the registrar.
 Live Events
 Objects of the Vaibhav Vyapaar IPO
Vaibhav Vyapaar plans to utilise Rs 32 crore from the net IPO proceeds to augment its capital base. The remaining proceeds will be allocated towards general corporate purposes.
 Financial performance
Vaibhav Vyapaar Ltd.'s total income increased 48% to Rs 38 crore in FY26 from Rs 25 crore in FY25. Its profit after tax (PAT) rose 33% to Rs 2 crore from Rs 1 crore over the same period.
 About Vaibhav Vyapaar
Incorporated in February 2009, Vaibhav Vyapaar Ltd. is a non-banking financial company ( NBFC ) that offers unsecured personal loans to salaried and self-employed individuals through its digital lending platform, LoanFront. Its mobile application facilitates the entire lending process, including customer verification, credit assessment, documentation, disbursal and repayment. The company also provides loans through direct lending and co-lending arrangements with other NBFCs and earns revenue by offering technology and application services to them.
The company uses technology-driven tools for credit assessment and risk evaluation and has operated its digital lending business through LoanFront for six years. It was acquired by CapFront Technologies Private Limited in October 2019. As of July 31, 2026, the company reported assets under management (AUM) of Rs 812.41 crore, a net worth of Rs 471.96 crore and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80. It had 56 employees across functions, including technology, operations and risk management.

docs.title: Tata will build what India needs, even if it takes longer: Tata Sons chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran
docs.text:
Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen

 Tata Sons chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran said on Tuesday that the conglomerate will continue making what the world and India require, including semiconductor chips , even if these take longer to build while the group continues to face a boardroom tussle.
 “Direction is certain, need is certain, ability to execute is certain,” Chandrasekaran said. at the 2026 Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi.
 Also Read: Tata Sons mulling legal view on Trusts offer, not seen as a Trusts resolution to be considered 
Chandrasekaran focussed on the fact that India has the talent, market and the ability to build, pressing that semiconductor chips would be fundamentally required in a world with growing space for advanced manufacturing.
At nearly 160 years old and with $185 billion in revenue last fiscal, Tata is betting $120 billion on its next growth chapter, anchored by India’s first chip-making unit, a landmark project in the country’s ambition to become a high-tech manufacturing powerhouse.
 Live Events
Noel Tata, chairman at Tata Trusts that owns about 66% of Tata Sons, has recently publicly had major differences with Chandrasekaran over the group's decisions pertaining to capital allocation and faster return to shareholders. The feud took a turn when Chandrasekaran was re-appointed as chairman of the conglomerate, a move that Noel Tata has not endorsed.
Separately, Tata Electronics has been building the country's first large-scale chip production plant and has faced major operational issues, according to a report by Bloomberg News.
Chandra has acknowledged that the company has been going through a rough time, while batting multiple operational matters and a boardroom tussle at the helm. The conglomerate-controlled flag carrier Air India faced a major crash last year, a cyberattack and major disruptions around its supply-chain. Despite these snags, the group has seen its margins holding and growth in double-digits.
 Also Read: Tata Trusts rift deepens: Noel Tata-led trustees say 'Trusts do not run Tata Sons' as they defend restructuring plan to avoid listing 
Chandra had announced in August that he would step down when his term ends in February next year, citing a lack of unanimous support from the board. The fault lines had surfaced months ago, when Noel Tata objected in February, prompting the board to postpone a decision on Chandra’s third term. The Tata Trusts accepted his decision and began the search for a successor.
But the succession question took a turn in September, when the Tata Sons board reappointed Chandra for another five years. Noel, one of the Trusts’ two nominees on the board, voted against the move. The Trusts subsequently challenged the reappointment as illegal under Tata Sons’ articles of association, citing legal advice. Tata Sons has rejected that interpretation, setting the stage for a potentially consequential legal battle over control of the conglomerate.

docs.title: Punjab truck driver keeps trying his luck every month for 2 years, wins Rs 1.3 crore lottery in Dubai
docs.text:
A 53-year-old truck driver from Punjab has won Dh500,000 (around Rs 1.3 crore) in Abu Dhabi's Big Ticket draw after trying his luck with a group of friends every month for nearly two years. Kulwant Singh, who has lived and worked in Dubai for 18 years, discovered that his latest lottery entry had won the prize, according to Gulf News . He works in the Jebel Ali area of Dubai and plans to use the money to support his family and invest in their home.
 Also Read: Woman buys 196 parking spaces for Rs 20 crore, residents sue after she doubles rental charges 
Singh's win was part of Abu Dhabi Big Ticket's Series 291 draw, in which five Indian expatriates collectively won Dh1.95 million in consolation prizes, the report said. 
 How Kulwant Singh won the Dubai lottery
Singh said he first learned about the lottery through online videos and decided to participate. For the winning draw, he selected a ticket at random, without knowing it would bring him such a large prize. The truck driver said he was delighted when he learned about the result. He and his friends had been buying tickets together every month for approximately two years.
"I was very happy when I found out that we had won. We purchase tickets together every month, so it was a wonderful feeling to finally receive the good news," he said, as quoted by Gulf News . The group continued participating in the draw over that period, hoping to win. Their latest entry finally brought them a reward.
 Live Events
 What does the Punjab truck driver plan to do with the prize money?
Unlike winners who may look for expensive purchases after receiving a windfall, Singh has identified a more personal priority. He wants to use the money to help his family and invest in their home. His plans reflect the importance of financial security for someone who has spent years working away from home.
"I want to use the money for my family and towards our home," Singh said, according to the report. He also indicated that he and his friends intend to continue participating in future draws.
 Kerala engineer also wins in the same draw
Singh was not the only Indian expatriate to receive good news from the Big Ticket draw. Muhammed Ijas C , a 30-year-old engineer from Kerala, won Dh100,000, equivalent to approximately Rs 26 lakh. Unlike Singh, Ijas chose his ticket number for a personal reason. He combined his son's birthdate and birth year to arrive at the number that eventually won him the prize.
"It was one of the most special moments for me. I had chosen the number based on my son's birthday, so finding out that we had won made it even more meaningful," he said, as quoted by Gulf News . The two winners had different approaches to selecting their entries. Singh picked his ticket randomly, while Ijas used a number connected to his family.
Their wins were among the prizes awarded in Series 291, which saw five Indian expatriates receive consolation prizes worth a combined Dh1.95 million.

As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.
 WATCH LIVE TODAY: Press conference with #FOMC Chair Powell at 2:30 p.m. ET: https://t.co/1uJrua5qsH https://t.co/FJa6TbkDMt pic.twitter.com/87g5NJITsz 
— Federal Reserve (@federalreserve) September 18, 2024 
By the end 2024, markets are expecting a total reduction of at least 100 basis points in the first rate cut cycle in over 4 years since 2020.
But whether the Fed goes for 25 or 50 bps, the biggest trigger for stock prices to move up or down would be Powell's motivation behind the cut.
Asset classes from stocks, currencies and fixed income could all log swings in the immediate aftermath of the Fed decision.
While easing US interest rates are directionally positive for equities in general, “we should keep in mind interest rates are just one variable in a complex adaptive system that determines the direction of Indian equity markets”, said Anoop Vijaykumar, Investments and Head of Research at Capitalmind.

HCL Technologies' strong Q2 earnings, accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) revenue and robust deal wins have strengthened the investment case for the IT stock, but concerns over valuations and the sustainability of a demand recovery could limit its upside. Brokerages remain divided on HCLTech's prospects after the company raised the lower end of its FY27 revenue growth guidance, with price targets suggesting potential returns ranging from an 11 percent decline to a 9 percent gain from Monday's closing price.
 HCLTech shares closed at Rs 1,223 on Monday, up 0.52 percent ahead of the earnings announcement. The stock has declined 25.2 percent so far in 2026, compared with a 14.5 percent fall in the Nifty 50. The company's market capitalisation stands at Rs 3.32 lakh crore.
 Nomura has maintained its Buy rating on HCLTech stock with a target price of Rs 1,330 , implying an upside of nearly 9 percent from Monday's closing price. The brokerage highlighted strong performance in the services business, continued growth in AI revenue and steady progress on the company's five-pillar AI strategy.
Nomura expects operating margins to normalise over FY27 and FY28 and has raised its earnings per share (EPS) estimates for the two financial years by around 2-3 percent. It also noted that the midpoint of HCLTech's FY27 revenue growth guidance remains unchanged.
 Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today 
However, HSBC maintained its Hold rating with a target price of Rs 1,225 , broadly in line with the stock's latest closing price. The brokerage said HCLTech's second-quarter results were largely in line with expectations. While management indicated an improvement in demand in recent weeks, HSBC noted that the sustainability of this recovery remains uncertain.
It also flagged the stock's premium valuation relative to peers, given its moderate outperformance and lower operating margins.
 CLSA has retained its Hold rating on HCLTech with a target price of Rs 1,094 , indicating a potential downside of about 11 percent from Monday's close. The brokerage said that revenue was broadly in line with expectations, while EBIT and EPS exceeded consensus estimates by 4 percent and 6 percent, respectively. CLSA highlighted the company's strong order book, growing advanced AI revenue and large deal wins, which could support market share gains.
However, it expects FY27 constant-currency revenue growth of 3 percent, towards the lower end of the company's revised guidance. The brokerage raised its FY27 EPS estimate by 2 percent.
HCLTech reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 5,132 crore for the September quarter, up 21.2 percent year-on-year and 11 percent sequentially. Revenue from operations rose 11.5 percent year-on-year to Rs 35,620 crore, while operating margin expanded 131 basis points sequentially and 71 basis points annually to 18.2 percent.
Advanced AI revenue surged 78 percent year-on-year and 28.4 percent sequentially to $219 million, underscoring the growing contribution of AI-led services. The company also reported net new deal wins worth $3.24 billion, including a $1.14 billion mega AI deal from Mercedes-Benz.
HCLTech revised its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 2.5-4 percent from 1-4 percent earlier, raising the lower end while keeping the midpoint unchanged. Its operating margin guidance was retained at 17.5-18.5 percent. The company also announced a Global Premier Partnership with Anthropic to accelerate enterprise adoption of agentic AI, focusing on safety, cybersecurity and governance.

RBL Bank shares plunged 8.5 percent to Rs 382 apiece on Tuesday, making the private lender the biggest loser on both the BSE 500 and Nifty 500 indices, despite reporting a nearly threefold increase in its fiscal second quarter net profit. The sharp selloff came as concerns over elevated credit costs, sluggish core retail loan growth and expensive valuations overshadowed improvements in profitability and net interest margins.
Brokerages remained divided on RBL Bank stock outlook following its Q2 FY27 results. Goldman Sachs and CLSA maintained bearish ratings with identical target prices of Rs 310, citing concerns over the pace of the turnaround and return ratios. However, Citi retained its bullish stance with a target price of Rs 505, betting on improving margins and strong earnings growth.
Despite Tuesday's decline, RBL Bank stock remains up 21.6 percent so far in 2026, significantly outperforming the Nifty 50, which has fallen 14 percent during the same period. The bank's market capitalisation stood at approximately Rs 59,500 crore.
RBL Bank reported a 169 percent year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to Rs 481.7 crore for the July-September quarter, while net interest income (NII) grew 37.4 percent to Rs 2,131 crore. Net interest margin (NIM) expanded to 4.61 percent from 4.13 percent sequentially.
 Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today 
Asset quality improved, with the gross NPA ratio declining to 1.02 percent from 1.30 percent in June. However, provisions rose to Rs 766.5 crore from Rs 599.2 crore sequentially, reflecting continued credit cost pressures. Net advances grew 42 percent year-on-year, while deposits increased 34 percent, aided by foreign currency non-resident (FCNR) inflows under the RBI's special scheme.
Goldman Sachs maintained its 'Sell' rating with a target price of Rs 310, implying 26 percent downside from Monday's close. Despite improvements in return on assets and return on equity to 0.9 percent and 4.4 percent, respectively, the brokerage flagged subdued core retail loan growth and fee income.
Goldman Sachs raised its FY28 and FY29 earnings estimates by 11 percent and 12 percent on stronger FCNR(B) flows but cautioned that the turnaround would be gradual, with valuations at 19 times FY28 earnings appearing expensive.
CLSA retained its 'Underperform' rating and Rs 310 target, noting that profit missed estimates by 15 percent due to higher credit costs. Despite $3.4 billion in FCNR deposit inflows, average CASA growth remained muted at 5 percent, while deposit costs stayed above peers. CLSA also flagged growth driven by lower-yielding loans, arguing that a medium-term return on equity of 8-9 percent did not justify the stock's 1.4 times price-to-book valuation.
Citi maintained its 'Buy' rating with a target price of Rs 505, implying 21 percent upside from Monday's close. It highlighted a 48-basis-point sequential expansion in NIM to 4.61 percent, driving NII growth of 37 percent year-on-year and 29 percent sequentially.
While credit costs rose to 2.52 percent amid provisions and credit card stress, Citi noted that card slippages eased to Rs 125-130 crore in September, compared with Rs 660 crore for the entire quarter. The brokerage expects card credit costs to normalise to around 6 percent in the second half of FY27 and forecasts earnings growth of over 35 percent in FY27 and more than 20 percent annually in FY28-29.

HCL Technologies shares surged over 8 percent on Tuesday, emerging as the top gainer on the Nifty 50 after the IT services major reported strong fiscal second quarter earnings, robust artificial intelligence (AI) revenue growth and large deal wins. The company also raised the lower end of its FY27 revenue growth guidance, although brokerages remain divided over the stock's upside potential.
HCLTech shares closed at Rs 1,326, up 8.42 percent from Monday's closing price of Rs 1,223. Despite Tuesday's rally, the stock remains down 18.9 percent so far in 2026, against a 13.1 percent decline in the Nifty 50. The company's market capitalisation stood at Rs 3.6 lakh crore.
The gains came amid a sharp rally in the broader market. At the close, the Sensex was up 1,109.10 points, or 1.54 percent, at 73,033.78, while the Nifty gained 358.60 points, or 1.60 percent, to 22,721.95. Market breadth was positive, with 2,386 shares advancing against 1,786 declining and 185 remaining unchanged.
 Also read | HCL Technologies stock outlook: AI growth, strong Q2 earnings offer upside potential, but there's a catch 
HCLTech on Monday reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 5,132 crore for the September quarter, up 21.2 percent year-on-year, while revenue rose 11.5 percent to Rs 35,620 crore. Operating margin expanded 131 basis points sequentially to 18.2 percent.
The company's advanced AI revenue surged 78 percent year-on-year to $219 million, while net new deal wins stood at $3.24 billion, including a $1.14 billion mega AI deal from Mercedes-Benz. HCLTech raised the lower end of its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 2.5 percent from 1 percent, retaining the upper end at 4 percent. Its operating margin guidance remained unchanged at 17.5-18.5 percent.

Brokerages offered mixed assessments of HCLTech's outlook following the results. Nomura maintained its Buy rating with a target price of Rs 1,330, citing strong services performance, rising AI revenue and progress on the company's AI strategy. The target implies an upside of about 4.6 percent from Tuesday's early trading price.
HSBC retained its Hold rating with a target price of Rs 1,225, highlighting uncertainty over the sustainability of improving demand and concerns about premium valuations. CLSA also maintained its Hold rating, with a target of Rs 1,094, despite acknowledging strong deal wins and AI-led growth opportunities.

 RBI determined to do what is necessary to ensure orderly rupee movement: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra
 RBI governor said the measures aimed to ensure forex markets serve genuine hedging needs rather than speculative bets. 
 October 13, 2026 / 21:43 IST 
 Story continues below Advertisement
 Remove Ad 
 RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra (File image) 
 RBI may take more steps to curb forex speculation if needed.
 Governor Sanjay Malhotra rules out capital control measures.
 External sector remains the primary macroeconomic challenge.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra told Moneycontrol that the central bank would consider further measures to curb speculative trading in the foreign exchange market if required.
“The RBI is determined to do whatever is necessary to ensure orderly movement in the foreign exchange market,” Malhotra said speaking exclusively to Moneycontrol, adding that the recent measures should not be interpreted as restrictions on capital flows.
 He said the measures aimed to ensure forex markets serve genuine hedging needs rather than speculative bets. The central bank had seen around one-third of forex derivative trades being cancelled on the same day, he said.
The governor described the external sector as India’s main macroeconomic challenge, despite robust domestic growth, healthy bank balance sheets and improving corporate earnings. He said the government and the RBI would take further steps, if necessary, to strengthen the country’s balance of payments. Edited excerpts:
 You announced a slew of measures over the weekend aimed at curbing speculative forex transactions. What was the immediate trigger for these measures? 
 The purpose of these measures is primarily to ensure that there is an orderly movement of the forex market. The measures that have been taken: for example, rebooking of cancelled forex derivative contracts have been disallowed. These will also check undue speculative bets. We have brought in a forex reserve requirement because we observed that there is excessive speculative positioning on the buy side. And the other major announcement is basically a re-articulation, mostly procedural, regarding the documentation required. The limits have also been decreased from $100 million to $5 million.
The primary purpose of our forex markets is to meet and hedge underlying foreign exchange requirements. Unlike equities, where participants can take a view on share price movements, forex markets are intended primarily for those with a genuine hedging requirement.
 Read More: RBI’s forex curbs not capital controls: Governor Sanjay Malhotra to Moneycontrol 
 Did you observe excessive speculation, and over what period of time did you see this trend? 
Over the past few months, we have observed a very high proportion of trades being cancelled and rebooked on the same day. In some cases, about one-third of trades were closed or cancelled on the day they were entered into. If a participant has a genuine underlying requirement, such as an import payment, they will typically maintain the hedge for the reasonable duration of that exposure. The high proportion of same-day cancellations and rebooking indicated a significant speculative element in the forex derivatives market. We have, therefore, taken these measures to curb such excessive speculation.
 We saw a strong appreciation in the rupee on Monday. Do you expect these measures to have a lasting impact on the rupee and stabilise INR at a certain level? 
We have repeatedly said that we do not target any particular price level or band for the rupee.
Our effort has always been to ensure orderly movement in the currency and prevent excessive speculation. We observed excessive volatility and one-sided bets that were preventing market forces from determining the rupee’s true value. That is why we have taken these measures.
India’s macroeconomic fundamentals are very strong, and I am confident that the country will emerge stronger from the current episode. The government has been proactive, and the corporate sector has repeatedly demonstrated resilience, using challenging periods as opportunities to strengthen the economy and the external sector.
I believe forex markets are getting unduly pessimistic about the Indian economy’s future, which is actually underpinned by strong economic fundamentals. The free trade agreements we have signed, measures to improve productivity, ease-of-doing-business reforms and schemes such as the production-linked incentive (PLI) programme should support productivity and help reduce imports.
We are also seeing robust inflows on the capital account. Remittances remain strong, services exports continue to perform well, and foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows are healthy. I am confident that FDI will also continue to support India’s balance of payments position.
 Read More: Markets overly pessimistic on rupee: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra tells Moneycontrol 
This is in no way a capital control measure. We have excluded all capital account transactions from the foreign exchange reserve ratio requirements as far as customers are concerned. Non-residents

 Stock market recap: Indian equities posted a strong rebound on Tuesday, led by a sharp rally in IT stocks after HCL Tech's quarterly results, as investors looked past higher inflation data. 
 Nifty 50 rose 358.60 points, or 1.60%, to close at the day’s high of 22,721.9, while Sensex gained 1,109.10 points, or 1.54%, to settle at 73,033.78. 
 IT was the standout sector, rising more than 3%, as HCL Tech jumped about 7% after strong profit growth, improved margins, and an upgrade to the lower end of its full-year revenue forecast. TCS gained around 6%, while Tech Mahindra and Infosys also rose. Hindustan Unilever and Bajaj Auto added about 3% each. Data released on Monday showed that retail inflation rose 5.54% in September from 4.83% in August, while food inflation climbed to 7.74%, keeping the possibility of further RBI rate hikes alive. Even so, domestic institutional buying helped absorb foreign selling, and a firmer rupee supported sentiment. Breadth was positive, with 2,128 stocks advancing, 1,418 stocks declining, and 98 remaining unchanged. Investors will now monitor upcoming quarterly earnings, crude oil prices above $100 per barrel, and foreign fund flows. 
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India: 
 Buy: eClerx Services Limited (current price: ₹ 1,961) 
 Why it’s recommended: Strong demand for AI-powered analytics, digital operations, automation, and business process transformation services from global Fortune 2000 clients across financial services, telecom, retail, and media sectors. Deep domain expertise and expanding GenAI/automation capabilities are helping drive higher-value engagements and long-term client relationships. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 24.04, 52-week high: ₹ 2,497.50, volume: ₹ 96.28 crore 
 Technical analysis: Reclaimed its 21-DMA on above-average volume 
 Risk factors : High dependence on clients in developed markets exposes revenue growth to global economic slowdown and discretionary technology spending cuts. Client concentration risk, where loss or downsizing of large enterprise accounts can materially impact revenues and margins.

 Target price : ₹ 2,280 in two to three days 
 Stop loss: ₹ 1,850 
 Buy: Coforge Limited (current price: ₹ 1,929)

AI-native strategy, proprietary platforms, and synergy from acquisitions are strengthening market position and driving faster growth than industry peers.

 Indian equities staged a strong recovery on Tuesday, with Nifty 50 rising 358.60 points, or 1.60%, to close at 22,721.95. The index opened at 22,364.15, briefly declined to 22,288.45, and then recovered steadily to close at the day’s high, signalling sustained buying interest through the session. Market breadth was positive, with 2,128 stocks advancing, 1,418 stocks declining, and 98 remaining unchanged, indicating broad participation across the market. Sectoral performance was led by IT (+5.22%), followed by Realty (+2.46%), and Financial Services (+1.54%). FMCG, PSU Banks, Auto, Metals and Consumer Durables also gained between 1.15% and 1.56%. Private Banks, Oil and Gas, Media, and Healthcare posted more modest advances, while Pharma was largely flat and mid-small healthcare declined marginally.

 Stock market recap: Indian equities gave up early gains and ended lower on Monday as rising bond yields and persistent foreign selling outweighed Friday's relief rally.  India's 10-year bond yield rose to a three-year high of about 7.37% after the RBI tightened banks' daily cash reserve rules to drain surplus liquidity. Foreign investors sold about ₹ 45,125 crore of Indian shares in October's first six sessions, nearly matching September’s total. Iran's rejection of the latest U.S. peace proposal and weak Asian markets added to the caution, although the rupee gained about 1% after the RBI's weekend steps to curb dollar demand. 
 FMCG was the weakest sector, falling 1.67% on losses in ITC, Dabur, and HUL, followed by PSU Banks and IT. Media rallied 4.60%, while Autos, Realty, and Pharma ended higher. The Nifty 50 climbed 1.6% to close at 22,721.95, while the BSE Sensex advanced 1.54% to 73,033.78. The Indian rupee strengthened to 95.28 against the US dollar, extending its recovery for a second consecutive session after the RBI unveiled additional measures to support the domestic currency. The Nifty IT index surged 5.2%, marking its biggest single-day gain since 12 May 2025. HCLTech jumped 8.4%, its sharpest daily percentage gain in more than six years, emerging as the biggest gainer on the index. The rally followed the company's quarterly results, which beat estimates, supported by an improvement in profitability metrics. Jay Thakkar of ICICI Securities has recommended Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) futures, Shree Cement futures and Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company (Chola Finance) futures for near-term trading opportunities. For M&M futures, Thakkar recommends buying in the ₹ 2,850– ₹ 2,870 range, with a stop-loss below ₹ 2,780. The targets are ₹ 3,000 and ₹ 3,070. For Shree Cement futures, he suggests buying in the ₹ 22,100– ₹ 22,150 range, with a stop-loss below ₹ 21,000. The stock has upside targets of ₹ 23,500 and ₹ 24,000. For Chola Finance futures, Thakkar recommends buying in the ₹ 1,610– ₹ 1,630 range, with a stop-loss below ₹ 1,575. The targets for the trade are ₹ 1,685 and ₹ 1,720. Jay Thakkar, Vice President and Head of Derivatives and Quant Research at ICICI Securities, said the Nifty 50's positive close in the previous session, following a weekly gain last week, has resulted in the formation of higher tops and higher bottoms, signalling a potential reversal from a downtrend to an uptrend. He noted that the short-term trend would remain positive as long as the index holds above 22,300, with upside targets of 23,000 and 23,200. Options data also supports the bullish outlook, with the put-call ratio (PCR) rising to 1.38 for the next weekly expiry. Significant put writing at 22,500 indicates immediate support, while 23,000 has the highest call open interest. A sustained move above this level could trigger further short covering, Thakkar said. He added that the premium in Nifty 50 futures has increased sharply to around 140 points from approximately 30 points in the previous session, indicating a rise in short-covering activity. Meanwhile, the India VIX has declined by more than 7% to around 14. As long as the volatility index remains below 16, the short-term bias is likely to stay positive, supporting a potential rebound towards 23,000–23,200, he said. Jay Thakkar of ICICI Securities recommends Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) Futures, Shree Cements Futures, and Cholamandalam Investment and Fin Co Futures. M&M has started to form higher tops and bottoms on the daily charts, and with that, open interest has decreased as well, indicating short covering. It closed in negative territory for 8 consecutive weeks, and now, with this reversal, it is expected to bounce back from this oversold region. As per the options data, 2,850 CE has a significant call base on an immediate basis, and a close above that will lead to further short covering. The max pain is at 2,900, and if the stock manages to surpass that level,there will be further short covering. Shree Cement has seen some short additions in the recent fall; however, with some consolidation, it has also seen some short covering, indicating that a bounce back is on the cards. As per the options data, the 22,000 strike has the highest call base, and the stock has closed above the same; hence, a further up move is expected from hereon. The max pain is also at 22,000 levels; hence, a close above that indicates a short-term reversal from down to up Chola Finance has also started forming higher tops and bottoms, and with that, the stock has witnessed an increase in open interest, which is a positive sign. It had fallen on account of long unwinding and with this reversal in the markets a bounce back cant be ruled out. There has been significant put additions at the lower levels from 1,540-1,620 strikes indicating support at the lower levels, on the upside 1,700 strike has the highest call base which is the minimum target. docs.title: Frenzied stock-options trading shows individual investors are still hungry for risk
docs.text:
Global 
 Frenzied stock-options trading shows individual investors are still hungry for risk
 Krystal Hur , Hannah Erin Lang , The Wall Street Journal 4 min read 13 Oct 2026, 06:39 AM IST 
 Summary
 Trading in single-stock options contracts are near levels reached in 2021, when a new generation of amateur investors shook up Wall Street. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Individual investors aren’t letting anything get them down these days.
 Their fervor is showing up in frenzied trading of options, or contracts that allow holders to buy or sell a stock at a set price, by a certain date. Volumes in options tied to individual stocks have recently reached levels seen during the meme-stock mania of 2021, about $700 billion of notional volume a day, according to Carrick Lane, an investment manager specializing in options strategies. The prices of call options, which give the right to buy, have eclipsed levels seen during that time.
 A new generation of individual investors discovered the markets during the post-Covid rally, and by early 2021 many amateur traders were pushing into more complicated, and often riskier, bets. A boom in stock options and other derivatives was under way.
 Those markets are now abuzz with retail activity once again, and Wall Street knows the reason: Individual investors are looking past rising interest rates, $100 oil prices and war in the Middle East . They are focusing on strong corporate earnings, and as comfortable rolling the dice on volatile markets as they were back when GameStop, Roaring Kitty and AMC Entertainment were the talk of Reddit forums.
 Bullishness among individual investors, as measured by the percentage who expect stock prices to rise over the next six months, reached 40.3% for the week ended Oct. 7, according to the latest survey from the American Association of Individual Investors. That is the highest level since mid-July and comparable to levels seen in 2021.
 Many, like 41-year-old Kunal Berry, are buoyed by the success of the artificial-intelligence trade and optimistic about the technology’s potential to transform business and the economy.
 “The growth is there,” the Los Angeles-based consultant said. Berry has chased gains in megacap tech names including Nvidia, Amazon and SpaceX. “The short-term volatility—you’ve just got to have the stomach for it,” he said.
 The meme-stock craze might have faded as many of the era’s favorite stocks eventually lost their luster. But individual investors’ enthusiasm for the markets has only grown stronger over the past five years. This cohort kept “buying the dip” even during April 2025, when a global trade war rattled professional investors and triggered a deep selloff. They helped crown a new class of AI darlings and piled into the SpaceX initial public offering. And they are still buying today.
 On Monday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.4%, or about 196 points. The S&P 500 fell less than 0.1% and the Nasdaq composite lost 0.4%.
 In another sign investors are feeling much as they did in 2021, more traders are comfortable betting on short-term price moves. More than half of current single-stock options volumes are concentrated in contracts less than two weeks away from expiring, according to John Marshall, a partner at Carrick Lane.
 One reason behind their persistent optimism is strong corporate profits, which have helped drive stocks to repeated records this year. Companies in the S&P 500 are expected to report earnings growth of about 30% for the third quarter from the prior year, according to FactSet. For 2026, profits are expected to jump 33%.
 Individual investors have grown a bit more selective in 2026, analysts say, opting to throw their weight behind a few high-conviction names over buying broader market dips. And retail activity slowed during the summer, following an explosive rally in shares of memory stocks and chip makers that peaked in June. But that summer cool-down historically tends to reverse in October, according to data from Citadel Securities—and DIY traders could be even more plugged in through the rest of the year.
 Not everyone is all-in on derivatives, either. But even more risk-averse investors are staying in the market.
 The top position bought by Charles Schwab’s clients in September was an exchange-traded fund tracking the Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index. That is the first time an ETF has taken that spot since Schwab began collecting that data in 2021. Clients also snapped up call options tied to ETFs last month, according to Schwab.
 “It’s a little bit more cautious optimism,” said Joe Mazzola, head trading strategist at Charles Schwab. “They’re definitely looking to buy dips.”
 Write to Krystal Hur at krystal.hur@wsj.com and Hannah Erin Lang at hannaherin.lang@wsj.com

docs.title: The mystery of the unknown sailor who inspired Trump to shake up the Navy
docs.text:
Global 
 The mystery of the unknown sailor who inspired Trump to shake up the Navy
 Marcus Weisgerber , The Wall Street Journal 6 min read 13 Oct 2026, 06:42 AM IST 
 Summary
 A chance encounter pushed the president to revamp the carrier fleet—and sent the Pentagon on a hunt for the elusive “Bill Jones.” 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 In August, President Trump directed the Navy to figure out how to return to using steam catapults on aircraft carriers to hurl fighter jets into the air.
 For U.S. military officials, the order marked the return of an old foe: Bill Jones.
 Who?
 Exactly. Trump has described the man as a “catapulter” who served in the Navy for 25 years and loves the smell of steam. Jones convinced Trump the old technology was superior to modern methods of launching jets, the president said.
 The incident sent Navy leaders searching for Jones to figure out what he said that prompted the president to demand an overhaul of one of the most expensive weapons programs in history. They never found him, according to defense officials.
 But they’re still dealing with the consequences of the mystery sailor and his chance encounter with the president.
 It all started just months into Trump’s first term when he was in Virginia touring the USS Gerald R. Ford, the newest aircraft carrier in the Navy’s fleet.
 This warship, the largest in the world and first in its class, cost about $19 billion but had experienced myriad problems over eight years of construction as cutting-edge, but unproven, technology was installed on the ship. It was years behind schedule and billions of dollars over budget.
 Trump seemed eager to apply his real-estate experience to the dazzlingly complex world of Pentagon procurement. He has said he grew tired of hearing excuses from the admirals and he wanted to hear from the people who operate the machinery.
 “I said, ‘Let me see the catapult people,’” Trump recalled during an April 2019 speech. “They said, ‘Sir, you don’t really want to do that?’ I said, ‘Yeah, those are the people that know what the hell they’re doing.’”
 Then it happened.
 The president said a sailor told him the Navy was making a mistake by ditching the tried-and-true method of using steam catapults. The decision to use an electromagnetic system to launch planes faster and more efficiently was dooming the service to failure.
 The USS Abraham Lincoln uses a steam catapult to conduct flight operations in the Arabian Sea. (US Navy)
 Trump has said the sailor told him if the electric catapults break you need geniuses from MIT to repair them, while the steam version can be fixed with a hammer and blowtorch. Industry officials said both descriptions vastly oversimplify things.
 After the encounter, Navy officials scrambled to explain to the president why the technologies were chosen and why removing them would be extremely disruptive, according to former defense officials.
 During a Thanksgiving call in November 2018 to sailors aboard the USS Ronald Reagan, an older Nimitz-class carrier with steam catapults, Trump asked the ship’s commanding officer his opinion of steam versus electric catapults.
 Then-Capt. Patrick Hannifin, now a three-star admiral in charge of naval forces in the Western Pacific and Indian Oceans, told Trump that while steam is reliable now, he preferred electromagnetic catapults.
 When Trump pressed Hannifin that “you have to be Albert Einstein” to operate them properly, the captain responded: “You sort of have to be Albert Einstein to run the nuclear power plants that we have here as well, but we’re doing that very well.”
 Trump said “that’s actually a very good answer.” The issue seemed to go away.
 It came roaring back as Trump sought and won re-election.
 He mentioned Jones by name during a January 2024 rally in Mason City, Iowa. Then in February 2025, Trump brought up the electric catapults when he swore in Tulsi Gabbard to be the director of national intelligence.
 There were rumors among industry insiders that Trump would sign an executive order telling the Navy to return to steam, but nothing happened—until this summer.
 In August, Trump signed a national security memorandum directing the Navy to figure out the cost and timeline for installing steam catapults and hydraulic elevators in the ship currently known as CVN 81, expected to join the fleet in 2034.
 The Navy isn’t getting its Ford-class carriers fast enough, and must simplify their design by using time- and battle-tested technology, an administration official said.
 It hasn’t built a carrier with steam since the USS George H.W. Bush, which entered the fleet in 2009.
 More problematic: “Steam catapults have been out of production for decades—no one makes them anymore,” said Hunter Stires, the maritime strategist to former Navy Secretary Carlos Del Toro.
 Since the order, Navy leaders have couched their public remarks.
 “If we were to go back to steam and hydraulics with the elevators, we need to really understand the total cost of that,” Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle said at a conference in Reno, according to USNI News. “That will be a significant design change.”
 He said a February stress test of the Ford’s electromagnetic launchers showed they outperformed their steam peers.
 An aircraft taking off via electric catapult on the USS Gerald R. Ford in January 2020. (Marcus Weisgerber/WSJ)
 Analysts and industry insiders say the new system could be more effective for future warfare since it could launch bomb-laden aircraft and drones. Shipbuilding experts worry putting steam back on a carrier would put the Navy technologically behind China.
 Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao has warned officials not to question the president’s decision.
 “To be clear, the debate on whether we do this has ended,” he wrote in an Aug. 28 memo, referring to a broader set of recommendations including the steam catapults.

docs.title: Nobel Prize 2026: Why Hall and Woodford’s economic research resonates in today’s world
docs.text:
Opinion 
 Nobel Prize 2026: Why Hall and Woodford’s economic research resonates in today’s world
 Mint Editorial Board 3 min read 13 Oct 2026, 07:30 AM IST 
 Summary
 This year’s Nobel Prize honours Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford, whose work draws upon microeconomic studies for a macro policy framework that holds special relevance in a world of high flux and economic shocks. Hear of ‘policy reflexivity,’ think of this duo. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 This year’s Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to Robert E. Hall of Stanford and Michael Woodford of Columbia for providing the “microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation.” 
 The citation says it all: the duo developed new macro models “that have significantly improved our ability to implement effective stabilisation policy.” Well-timed fiscal and monetary policy measures based on these models “can reduce the economy’s peaks and troughs.” 
 As the awarding panel’s chair John Hassler noted, the laureates’ work has been of good use to central banks and governments in securing an economy from shocks like energy price spikes and sudden shifts in retail demand. 
 The interesting part this year is the award’s recognition of work that uses micro analysis—at the level of firms and households—for a macro policy framework. The important part is the resonance that research by Hall and Woodford holds in today’s world of frequent economic shocks. 
 The panel puts it well: “The stabilization of aggregate economic activity is a central goal of economic policy.” This is especially so since such flux rarely hits people evenly; both recessions and inflation hit the poor harder. 
 The relationship between key aggregate variables like inflation, unemployment and GDP were broadly mapped at a macro level, with a major role played by Keynes, best known for making a case for intervention in an economy. 
 Today, policies to smoothen economic cycles are par for the course. The trouble was that the inner workings of those links were mostly a “ black box ,” in the panel’s words. Hall and Woodford helped open it up by delving into micro theory. 
 The former focused on demand and the latter on supply. Hall found that while household buying did depend on factors like expectations of the future, changes in it were unpredictable—like a ‘random walk.’ 
 In a 1978 article, he showed that a theory of consumption-smoothing—the idea that consumers prefer to keep it stable over time—worked well for grasping movements in overall consumption captured by data. However, unforeseeable shocks implied that consumption could not be as easily manipulated by government policy as was once thought, thus potentially limiting the effects of macro policy. 
 On his part, Woodford became the key architect of the so-called New Keynesian model: a full macro stabilization framework that has become the main tool for policymakers today. 
 He studied key micro conditions that made the market mechanism rigid. Sticky prices, for example. Businesses usually do not vary prices on a daily basis as demand and supply fluctuate; instead they adjust prices in discrete steps based on various calculations. These adjustments are also forward-looking. Woodford examined micro-level behaviour and used its learnings to formulate his new model for the use of policy tools. 
 While his original work was meant to sharpen monetary-policy analysis, the foundation it laid became a major tool for the analysis of fiscal policy as well. 
 The duo’s work can be said to have inspired today’s market notion of ‘reflexivity’ or awkward feedback loops adding complexity to macro policies. 
 Together, this year’s winners showed how aptly used fiscal and monetary policy can improve welfare by acting as a shock absorber. At a time of high uncertainty, with folks worried about the ability of authorities to cushion hard blows, the academic exertions of Hall and Woodford deserve policy-level attention.

 The Mint Editorial Board is a panel of editorial writers with expertise across diverse domains of relevance to the newspaper’s opinion readers. The Board draws on long years of experience in business, financial and economic journalism, apart from other professional fields, although each member’s record of coverage, analysis and commentary would reveal far broader interests. This panel keeps itself in tune with the news as it unfolds and aims to reflect Mint’s views, but cannot claim a daily consensus on every issue of debate that matters. 
As a matter of routine, the Mint Editorial Board produces the newspaper’s Quick Edit, a snappy daily comment on pressing issues, and Our View, a full-length editorial on an issue that demands urgent attention. These are often matters of policy but cover a lot more, as readers may attest. The Board’s mission in expressing opinions, done in the spirit of a "nation in conversation with itself", is aligned with that of Mint: to be "an unbiased and clear-minded chronicler of the Indian Dream".

 AI, bond yields, cyber top IMF risks to global financial markets
 Reshma Kapadia , Barrons 2 min read 13 Oct 2026, 04:26 PM IST 
 Summary
 Rising fiscal deficits could make it harder for governments to meet their financial obligations and handle risks of the future. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 The International Monetary Fund warned countries not to become complacent about their growing economies, noting rising risks to global financial markets from a bust in the artificial-intelligence market trade, rising sovereign bond yields and cyberattacks and underlying vulnerabilities in the financial system.
 As policymakers meet in Bangkok for the IMF’s annual meeting, economists highlighted vulnerabilities underneath what has been resilience in most asset markets over the past year and advised policymakers to bolster their cyber defenses and to limit fiscal deficits so that governments can make good on their financial obligations.
 Even amid a series of shocks to the world economy from war, trade friction and a bond rout in France, investors have taken comfort in the relative health of global banks. But IMF economists Athanasios Vamvakidis and Jason Wu note that while the core of the financial system is resilient overall, there are weak links.
 More than a fifth of global banking assets are likely to emerge with post-stress capital ratios that fall under regulatory limits for capital reserves—up 18% from a year ago, the duo write.
 Plus, the links between the banks and nonbank financial intermediaries—like pensions and insurers—are growing, such as through increased use of direct lending. Pension funds and insurers have also increased allocations to illiquid assets and derivatives and are relying often on the same asset managers.
 “This increases the risk that at a time of stress, they could face sudden liquidity needs through margin calls and could react in similar ways—for example by selling the same assets—amplifying market moves,” the duo cautions. “Some of these institutions also hold illiquid private credit, another potential amplification channel. At the same time, as borrowers have become more leveraged, some direct lending funds have committed to provide funding on demand. If financial conditions tighten, borrowers could draw on those facilities just as the funds that provide them could be facing their own liquidity pressures.”
 Recent global shocks, like the war in Iran and trade battles, have also diminished buffers to handle the potential fallout from higher interest rates or cyberattacks, which the IMF sees as a major risk. The International Monetary Fund also sees rising risks of AI investment and profitability not meeting expectations.
 The IMF highlighted concerns about the so-called AI trade, noting about $300 billion in equity investments and $650 billion in debt in exchange for $1.4 trillion in future revenue commitments in more than a dozen deals that they reviewed since 2023. “Circular financing arrangements in the AI sector, involving equity and debt flows between AI firms, suggest that stress at key companies receiving investment could lower revenue forecasts and investment valuations, which in turn would weaken the value of the accumulated debt in those deals,” the two IMF economists write.
 This comes against a backdrop of rising sovereign debt yields and as cybersecurity emerges as a growing risk. For example, the economists note, software providers had almost no time to deal with the vulnerabilities in more than 70% of reported cases year to date before attackers were able to capitalize on security flaws.
 Saddled with high government debt, re-emerging inflation pressures and higher borrowing costs, policymakers have less room to maneuver in the event of a shock. IMF economists are advising policymakers prioritize getting debt onto a sustainable path, bolstering cyber defense capabilities and limiting leverage and equity mismatches in AI, private credit and other nonbank areas.

Technical view: Chandan Taparia bullish on HAL, Shriram Finance & 1 more
 Chandan Taparia has said Nifty has given an inside bar breakout in the previous session, indicating a strong recovery. If Nifty holds above 22,700, it may bounce towards 22,850 and then 23,000 levels.
 Technical view: Chandan Taparia bullish on HAL, Shriram Finance & 1 more
 Chandan Taparia Mumbai 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 14 2026 | 8:02 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion. 
 Chandan Taparia, head derivatives & technicals, wealth management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd 
 Nifty index opened on a flattish note and bulls took charge right from the first tick itself. Any small dips were absorbed by the buyers. Momentum accelerated in the second half as the index surpassed its key hurdle of 22,550 zones and managed to sustain above the same. It formed a bullish candle on the daily chart and also gave an inside bar breakout indicating a strong recovery in buying momentum. Now it has to hold above 22,700 zones for a bounce towards 22,850 then 23,000 levels while on the downside support is seen at 22,600 then 22,500 levels.
 On option front, Maximum Call OI is at 23,000 then 23,200 strike while Maximum Put OI is at 22,500 then 22,600 strike. Call writing is seen at 23,000 then 23,100 strike while Put writing is seen at 22,500 then 22,600 strike. Option data suggests a broader trading range in between 22,300 to 23,200 zones while an immediate range between 22,500 to 23,000 levels.
 Bank Nifty index opened on a flattish note and gradually extended the momentum towards 55,500 zones in the latter part of the session. It formed a bullish candle on daily scale as buying interest was visible at lower levels but is still hovering near its 20 DEMA. FPIs favour IPOs over listed stocks for 3rd year running; will trend last?
 In 2026 alone, FPIs have poured in ₹55,524 crore into the primary market, while selling in the secondary market hit a record ₹3.15 trillion till September so far.
 Illustration: Binay Sinha
 Saloni Goel New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 14 2026 | 8:07 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 While foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have been net sellers in the secondary market over the past three years, they have continued to pour money into primary markets, signalling a clear preference for IPOs even as they pare their exposure to listed stocks.
 In 2026 alone, FPIs have poured in ₹55,524 crore into the primary market, while selling in the secondary market hit a record ₹3.15 trillion till September so far, according to Prime Database data.
 In the last two years, too, FPI flow trend has followed the same trajectory. For instance, in 2025, they sold Indian stocks worth ₹2.40 trillion but bought IPO market shares worth ₹73,910 crore. In 2024, their selling on Dalal Street was ₹1.21 trillion and buying in the IPO market was ₹1.22 trillion, helping clock positive FPI flows for the year of ₹427 crore. 
 The two markets clearly do not move in tandem.
 What explains this trend?
 While it is often believed that secondary market moves have a rub-off effect on the primary market, the same does not appear to be true.

 Apurva Sheth, head of market perspectives and research at SAMCO Securities, said part of this trend is structural in nature. In the primary market, FPIs can only buy; they can sell only if they hold a stake through pre-IPO, private equity, or venture capital investments. "At worst, FIIs stop buying; they rarely become sellers."
 FPIs have remained net buyers in India's primary market in every calendar year since December 2009, except 2011, when NSDL began reporting the split.
 Additionally, Sheth said that many platforms, such as fintech and new-age manufacturing businesses, are unavailable in the secondary market, so FIIs are churning out of slower-growth listed companies into high-growth names coming to market.
 FIIs are participating where they see a specific company, valuation or allocation opportunity, not necessarily making a broad bullish call on Indian equities, said Devarsh Vakil, Head of Research, HDFC Securities.
 Apart from access to booming sectors, analysts believe time spent is another consideration for FPIs. Prasenjit Paul of 129 Wealth Fund said a meaningful part of IPO participation is tactical, where FPIs look for quick listing gains, while secondary-market buying is generally done with a longer holding period. Check - TOP GAINERS NSE | TOP LOSERS NSE 
 Can Jio IPO mark primary market top?
 "As long as IPOs are priced rationally, investors will continue to participate for short-term listing gains, and that demand itself encourages more companies to enter the market. The record number of IPOs in 2026 is showing the market’s capacity to absorb new supply," he said.
 Going ahead, analysts said that IPO pricing will decide if the sentiment sustains. 
 "If future issues are priced for perfection into a risk-off market, the IPO cycle could turn sharply colder; if they are priced realistically, they may restore confidence in India’s primary market," Vakil said.
 Currently, the IPO pipeline remains healthy with Reliance Jio's mega IPO set to hit the market. According to multiple reports, Jio IPO could open as soon as October-end. 
 After the Jio IPO , the primary market could face some strain, since giant issues like NSE and Reliance pull heavy money out of the system, cautioned Prathamesh Kadival, research analyst at Bonanza. Such large offers soak up liquidity that smaller companies depend on, leaving thinner demand for them, he added.
 "Investors may also turn choosy, backing only the big names while ignoring the rest. So a short reversal looks possible, with weaker IPOs struggling for support. Still, if domestic inflows stay strong, the market should absorb the load and bounce back from it," according to the Bonanza analyst. Mid, smallcap MF assets hit ₹10 trillion; experts see momentum sustaining
 In September, smallcap funds saw a record net inflow of Rs 9,039 crore, while midcap funds attracted Rs 7,835 crore
 premium 
 So far this year, smallcap funds have seen net inflows of Rs 55,300 crore, while midcaps have seen flows of Rs 51,295 crore. In comparison, largecap funds have attracted only Rs 11,690 crore.
 Kairavi Lukka Abhishek Kumar Mumbai 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 14 2026 | 6:03 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Mid and smallcap schemes are now a Rs 10-trillion segment within the mutual fund (MF) industry, with assets under management (AUM) quadrupling in five years.
 This has been driven by strong investor inflows and mark-to-market gains from a sustained broader market rally.
 Active mid and smallcap funds had a combined AUM of Rs 9.8 trillion at the end of September 2026 compared to Rs 2.5 trillion in September 2021. In the same period, their combined share in active equity AUM rose from 19.6 per cent to 26 per cent. Experts see the growth momentum sustaining. The industry currently manages another Rs 35,000 crore through passive mid and smallcap funds. Investor appetite for these two relatively high-risk categories has risen over the past four years, buoyed by strong returns.
 Interest has picked up further in recent months as the broader market rebounded sharply after March 2026.
 In September, smallcap funds saw a record net inflow of Rs 9,039 crore, while midcap funds attracted Rs 7,835 crore.
 So far this year, smallcap funds have seen net inflows of Rs 55,300 crore, while midcaps have seen flows of Rs 51,295 crore. In comparison, largecap funds have attracted only Rs 11,690 crore.
 Valuations show a mixed story. While the Nifty Smallcap 250 index, the smallcap benchmark, is currently trading at 30.9 times trailing 12 months (TTM) price-to-earnings (P/E), it is at a premium to its five-year average P/E of 28.2 times. It remains lower than its 10-year average of 34 times. However, at 30.6 times P/E for the mid-cap benchmark, the Nifty Midcap 150 index, it is still cheaper than its five-year and 10-year averages of 33.5 times and 36.9 times respectively. The Nifty 50 is trading at 20.1 times P/E, lower than its five- and 10-year average price to earnings ratios. Yet, money managers are not too keen to write off small and midcap indices.
 Vipul Bhowar, executive director and head of equities at Waterfield Advisors, said he doesn’t expect flows into mid and smallcaps to moderate soon. “Despite elevated valuations, we believe valuations remain reasonable relative to growth. These are also segments where companies have invested meaningfully in growth over the past three years, and that investment is now beginning to pay off,” he said. 
 “With sufficient new supply, including most of the recent initial public offerings (IPOs), the segment has been able to absorb domestic inflows.”
 Broader markets have also outperformed the Nifty in 2026, as rampant foreign selling, and global geopolitical pressures have weighed more on the Bluechips. 
 The Nifty has declined 13.1 per cent in 2026 so far, while the Midcap 150 is down 2.4 per cent. The Nifty Smallcap 250 has gained nearly 7 per cent this year.
 “Valuations in these segments are somewhat above comfort levels following the recent run-up. This is partly justified by stronger earnings growth and relatively lower exposure to geopolitical and macro concerns weighing on largecaps,” said Harsh Gupta Madhusudan, fund manager and India equity strategist, Ionic Wealth.
 However, fund managers do not see the trend changing anytime soon.
 Mayur Shah, portfolio management services (PMS) fund manager at Anand Rathi Advisors said while largecaps now offer more comfortable valuations, he doesn't expect a wholesale shift away from mid and smallcaps.
 “The segment continues to offer stronger growth prospects, which remains a key attraction for investors,” he said.
 He added, “Valuations in themes such as power, automation, artificial intelligence (AI), data centres and defence have become stretched, but investor interest remains over their growth potential and relative attractiveness versus other asset classes.”

HCLTech's next test: Sustaining margins, deal momentum amid rich valuations
 Healthy new deal wins and traction in its artificial intelligence (AI) business also lifted investor sentiment. The stock was the top gainer in both the Nifty 50 and the Sensex, closing at ₹1,321
 premium 
 JP Morgan Research is underweight on the stock, believing that slower organic growth at the midpoint of the guidance range calls into question HCLTech’s premium multiples
 Ram Prasad Sahu 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 13 2026 | 10:25 PM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Robust services revenue growth, better-than-expected margin performance, and steady guidance helped shares of HCLTech, the country’s third-largest information technology services company by market capitalisation, gain 8.28 per cent on Tuesday.
 Healthy new deal wins and traction in its artificial intelligence (AI) business also lifted investor sentiment. The stock was the top gainer in both the Nifty 50 and the Sensex, closing at ₹1,321.
 Driven by the services and engineering research and development (ER&D) segments, the company reported quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q) revenue growth of 2.3 per cent in constant currency terms to $3.7 billion. The services business, which accounts for three-fourths of revenue, grew 3 per cent sequentially, including inorganic contributions from HPE’s telecommunications (telecom) solutions business and Jaspersoft.
 While inorganic growth contributed 97 basis points (bps) to overall revenue growth, the growth rate excluding acquisitions was 2.3 per cent. The ER&D business grew a robust 4.1 per cent, supporting overall growth. The product business, however, weighed on the top line, with revenue declining 5.8 per cent.
 Management raised its revenue growth guidance for 2026-27 (FY27) to 2.5-4 per cent from 1-4 per cent and its services revenue growth guidance to 3-4.5 per cent from 1.5-4.5 per cent, both in constant currency terms. The organic growth midpoint remains broadly unchanged, with the 50 bps increase in the overall guidance driven by inorganic contributions. 
 According to HDFC Securities, the guidance implies no acceleration in the second half of FY27, as management refrained from extrapolating a few weeks of strong demand amid a fluid business environment.
 Even as the macroeconomic (macro) environment remains uncertain, the deal pipeline remained healthy, with the company reporting net new bookings of $3.3 billion for the quarter. This was 35 per cent higher sequentially and 27 per cent higher year-on-year, marking the second-highest quarterly bookings figure and the company’s strongest first half to date.
 The $1.14 billion mega deal, won in July, is expected to start contributing in the first quarter of 2027-28 (FY28), rather than the third (October-December/Q3) or fourth quarter (January-March/Q4) of FY27, which provides revenue visibility. The company indicated that demand remained healthy, with a broad-based pipeline across verticals and geographies, although management remained cautious amid volatile external conditions.
 According to Axis Securities analysts Kuber Chauhan and Abhishek Bhalotia, the outlook is supported by a healthy deal pipeline across business verticals, continued AI implementation, and strategic partnerships. The brokerage believes HCLTech is well positioned for a stronger recovery following its restructuring initiatives and as AI adoption broadens across business verticals, provided the macro environment remains stable. It has a ‘buy’ rating on the stock, with a target price of ₹1,360.
 Alongside healthy deal bookings, margin performance also exceeded estimates. The earnings before interest and tax (Ebit) margin rose to 18.1 per cent, up 130 bps Q-o-Q and 70 bps from a year earlier. The improvement was well above estimates and was driven by gains of 73 bps from AI efficiencies and Project Ascend, 50 bps from operating leverage, 32 bps from higher-margin advanced AI revenues, and 23 bps from foreign exchange gains.
 These gains were partly offset by headwinds of 25 bps from the HPE telecom acquisition and 22 bps from restructuring costs. The company said AI services revenues carry margins 7-10 per cent higher than its overall company average. It retained its FY27 Ebit margin guidance of 17.5-18.5 per cent, which includes 40-50 bps in restructuring costs.
 Nomura Research has raised its FY27 Ebit margin estimate by 50 bps to 18 per cent. It has also increased its FY27-28 earnings per share estimates by 2-3 per cent to factor in the Q2 results and raised its target price to ₹1,330.
 Despite these positives, some brokerages remain cautious on the stock given its premium valuation. HSBC Research has a ‘hold’ rating, arguing that HCLTech trades at a premium to peers despite moderate outperformance and lower margins.
 JP Morgan Research is underweight on the stock, believing that slower organic growth at the midpoint of the guidance range calls into question HCLTech’s premium multiples.
 Citi Research says the sustainability of margins will be key and has a ‘sell’ rating, observing that the stock trades at a 20-25 per cent premium to Tata Consultancy Services and Infosys.
