docs.title: BHEL to Solar Industries: Nuvama’s Q2 playbook picks top capital goods & defence stocks
docs.text: Think of India’s big industrial companies as runners in the same race, but not on the same track. Some are building power lines across deserts, some are making the heavy machines that keep electricity flowing, and some are supplying the country’s armed forces. In its outlook for the Q2FY27, the brokerage house Nuvama sees opportunities across power equipment, infrastructure and defence. It prefers names such as Kalpataru Projects International (KPIL), Skipper, Bharat Heavy Electricals (BHEL), Solar Industries India and GE Vernova T&D India, based on their growth prospects, valuations and expected improvement in execution. KPIL and Skipper: Can the second half bring a recovery? EPC companies have faced execution challenges, partly due to disruptions in the Middle East. However, Nuvama believes the sector could be moving towards a recovery, even though the September quarter may not mark a clear turning point. ALSO READ5 Stocks Where FIIs Increased Their Stakes in Q2FY27 The brokerage expects KPIL to report revenue growth of 9% year-on-year, with an EBITDA margin of 8.9%. Skipper, which has no Middle East exposure in its order book, is expected to post revenue growth of 11.5% and a margin of 10.8%. Nuvama identifies domestic transmission and distribution demand, healthy buildings and factories orders, and improving export payment inflows as potential drivers of a second-half recovery. It also expects better working capital management to support cash flows. As per the brokerage report, “We believe the EPC pack is past the worst, although Q2 is unlikely to mark an inflection as ME disruptions weigh on execution and T&D margins.” Nuvama retains its ‘Buy’ rating on KPIL and Skipper. It values KPIL at 14.6 times estimated FY28 earnings per share (EPS), against a target multiple of 16 times and a bull-case multiple of 18 times. Skipper is valued at around 17 times earnings, compared with Nuvama’s target multiple of 20 times. Siemens Energy India and Voltamp Transformers: Margin recovery in focus High-voltage transmission and distribution (T&D) companies are expected to maintain strong operational performance. Nuvama estimates execution growth of 45.6% year-on-year, while operating profit margins could expand by 270 basis points to 22.4%. The brokerage notes that “HV T&D is expected to sustain its robust execution momentum, with execution growth of 45.6% YoY and blended margin expanding 270bp YoY to 22.4%.” However, with several stocks in this segment trading close to their target valuations, Nuvama prefers GE Vernova T&D India, identified as Siemens Energy in the report, due to its valuation, earnings growth and business portfolio. Among non-power industrial companies, the brokerage expects sequential margin improvement as earlier price hikes begin to flow through. It estimates order inflow and revenue growth of 19.4% and 13.1%, respectively, although margins could remain 220 basis points lower year-on-year. ALSO READDivi’s to Sai Life: Jefferies outlines 4 CRDMO stocks positioned to capture global orders Nuvama noted, "We like Voltamp on expected margin recovery, robust order inflows supported by new capacity expansion". It cites a valuation of 26 times earnings against a target multiple of 30 times. BHEL: Earnings growth could support the stock BHEL is another company on Nuvama’s list. The brokerage expects better operating margins as the company executes orders with higher profitability and benefits from operating leverage. Nuvama report added, “We also like BHEL on stronger OPM driven by execution of better margin orders and operating leverage.” Nuvama estimates BHEL’s EPS to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 76% between FY26-FY28. Solar Industries and BEL: Defence stocks remain in focus In the defence segment, Nuvama continues to prefer Solar Industries India and Bharat Electronics (BEL). It expects Solar Industries to benefit from defence execution, while BEL is expected to maintain operating margins above 27%. The brokerage says, “We expect Q2FY27 to sustain healthy execution momentum, with BEL maintaining 27%+ margin and SOIL benefiting from strong defence execution.” Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL) remains dependent on the pace of Light Combat Aircraft deliveries, while Bharat Dynamics (BDL) could see a sequential recovery as production and deliveries of the Akash Weapon System gather pace. Nuvama estimates Solar Industries’ EPS to grow at a CAGR of 46% between FY26-28. It cites a valuation of around 44 times earnings against a target multiple of 60 times. What investors need to watch Nuvama’s outlook highlighted three factors such as order execution, margin recovery and cash generation. EPC companies could benefit from stronger domestic demand and improving working capital, while high-voltage T&D businesses are expected to sustain execution. In defence, the pace at which orders translate into deliveries will remain important. The views, target prices, and recommendations expressed are those of the respective brokerage firms and do not reflect the official policy or position of Financial Express. This should not be construed as an offer, solicitation, or recommendation to buy or sell securities. Investors must conduct their own independent due diligence and seek advice from a SEBI-registered financial advisor before making any investment decisions.

docs.title: HCLTech jumps 5%: Nomura sees 9% upside but Nuvama warns of unfavourable risk-reward
docs.text: The share price of HCL Technologies surged nearly 5% in early trade today, October 13. The company is in focus after it declared its earnings for the second quarter of financial year 2027 (Q2FY27). The HCLTech share price rose to a high of Rs 1,282.7 apiece in early trade today. For Q2 FY27, HCL Tech posted its net profit at Rs 5,132 crore, rising 11% quarter-on-quarter. Its revenue was Rs 35,620 crore, up 3% QoQ. The company’s earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) margin was at 18.2%, rising 131 basis points QoQ and 71 bps YoY. Japanese brokerage Nomura has raised its target price for the stock after the results on strong performance in the services segment and continued growth in artificial intelligence-led revenues. However, brokerage Nuvama Institutional Equities sees only a marginal upside. ALSO READIndia’s telecom equipment market could double to $50 Bn: 3 stocks making 5G gear Nomura on HCLTech: Strong services performance Nomura maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock and increased its price target 1.5% to Rs 1,330 apiece. This implies an upside of nearly 9% from the stock’s closing price of Rs 1,223 on Monday. The brokerage also raised its FY27 and FY28 estimated earnings per share (EPS) view by 2-3% to factor in the Q2FY27 earnings performance. Nomura has marginally raised its revenue growth estimate for the company, in dollars, to 3-5.9% year-on-year in FY27-FY28. HCLTech revised its revenue growth guidance to 3-4% for services from 1.5-4.5%. For the overall company, it revised revenue growth guidance to 2.5-4% from 1-4% earlier. “This includes inorganic contribution of 62bp (basis points) and 87bp for services and overall company, respectively. HCLTech clarified that the mega deal (USD1bn+) won in early July would ramp up meaningfully only in 1QFY28E. Additionally, according to management, the anticipated weakness in top telco accounts and a top manufacturing account has played out and discretionary demand in telcos remains uncertain,” Nomura said. The company noted steady progress across the five key pillars of its AI strategy. It said advanced AI revenues are around 6% of annualised revenues and that two of its recently won large advanced AI deals were sourced through partner relationships. Nuvama on HCLTech: Unfavourable risk-reward Nuvama Institutional Equities has maintained its ‘Hold’ rating on the stock and its target price of Rs 1,250 is also unchanged. This implies a mere upside of 2%. The company’s services business is quite stable but the software business is dragging overall growth, Nuvama said, adding that the risk to reward is unfavourable as it is already at a 20% premium to TCS or Infosys, with a similar growth. ALSO READPoonawalla Fincorp up 8% on Q2 profit surge; Jefferies, Motilal see 23% upside potential “While it continues to do reasonably well—the narrowing growth differential, software segment drag and margin headwinds limit the upside potential,” Nuvama said. HCLTech appears to reach close to the mid-point of its margin guidance, though further expansion in FY28 might be hampered by the large auto segment deal. HCLTech share price: What next for investors Overall, HCLTech has maintained the upper band of their FY27 revenue guidance at 4%. The lower band has been raised to 2.5% from 1% earlier. The management indicated that they are optimistic about the outlook ahead and added that demand was healthy towards the end of the quarter. However, it remained cautious given the fluid macro environment. The rupee and global headwinds will also be in focus and it will be interesting how it impacts the next two quarters. docs.title: Stop tracking FII outflows: Why Kotak says valuations, not ‘flows’, drive stock prices
docs.text: One of the biggest points of discussion in the market is the sharp spike in FII selling in the recent few weeks. In 8 days of October they have net sold over Rs 40,000 crore in equities and this follows the net Rs 45,000 crore outflow in September. On the other hand, domestic institutional investors have been steady buyers. Is this big divergence in flows really responsible for the price action in the stock market? The brokerage house Kotak Institutional Equities, in its report dated October 12, 2026, pointed out that investors should focus more on company valuations, earnings expectations and business prospects than on daily investment flow trends. As per the brokerage house, the excessive attention given to market flows, share ownership and price movements has distracted investors from the most important question, that is, whether a stock is worth its current price. “We reiterate that ‘flows’ are irrelevant for stock price movements,” said Sanjeev Prasad, MD & Co-Head of Kotak Institutional Equities. He added that, “a stock price is simply the aggregate view of the market at a point in time. Any change in expectations about earnings will change future EPS estimates, and any change in expectations about future prospects will change P An investor will buy based on positive changes to expectations and sell based on negative changes to expectations—buying or selling follows the change in expectations.” ALSO READ5 Stocks Where FIIs Increased Their Stakes in Q2FY27 Kotak in its report argued that without understanding a company's underlying value, investors risk buying stocks simply because prices are rising or selling them because prices are falling. Here is a detailed analysis of the Kotak perspective on what really drives share price movements and what investors must watch out for - Why Kotak questions the market flow theory Kotak argues that buying and selling in the secondary market does not, by itself, explain why stock prices change. When one investor sells shares, another investor buys them. The transaction transfers ownership of the shares and cash between the two parties, but it does not change the company's total number of outstanding shares. The brokerage noted, "As a corollary, investors can stop attributing market movements to ‘flows’, lamenting FPI outflows or fretting about domestic inflows." Can money really move between stocks and sectors? Investors often hear that money is moving from information technology stocks to banking shares, or from large-cap companies to mid-cap and small-cap stocks. Kotak questions whether such explanations adequately describe market behaviour. According to the brokerage report, transactions involve buyers and sellers exchanging shares and cash. Differences in stock performance are better understood by examining company fundamentals, valuations and changing investor expectations. Do large IPOs drain money from the stock market? Initial public offerings (IPOs) are sometimes blamed for reducing liquidity in the secondary market, where investors buy and sell already-listed shares. Kotak argues that this explanation also overlooks the role of valuations and investor demand. According to the brokerage, "We would ignore market worries about large IPOs affecting liquidity (whatever that may mean) in the secondary market for the aforementioned reasons. Money cannot ‘move out’ of the secondary to the primary market, as there is no money in the secondary market anyway." ALSO READRs 41,000 crore gone in 8 days: 3 reasons why FII selling spree gathered momentum The report also noted that India's annual household financial savings are substantially larger than IPO issuances, while foreign portfolio investors have participated actively in the primary market. Earnings and valuations: What really drives stock prices? Kotak identifies earnings expectations and valuation multiples as the key factors influencing share prices. The brokerage added, "Earnings are relevant in the long term and multiples in the short term for stock prices." If investors expect a company to earn more in the coming years, its estimated earnings per share could rise, supporting a higher share price. However, if investors become less willing to pay a premium for those earnings, the price-to-earnings multiple may contract. Kotak added, "Without the anchor of value, market sentiment will reflect, and investing will largely comprise chasing rising or falling prices." The views, target prices, and recommendations expressed are those of the respective brokerage firms and do not reflect the official policy or position of Financial Express. docs.title: Is Kotak Mahindra Bank a ‘Buy’ After Anup Saha’s Appointment? Analysts Weigh In
docs.text: The Kotak Mahindra Bank share price has been in focus after the appointment of Anup Saha as the new Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the bank. While the 1-year return is less than 1%, the stock has delivered double-digit returns in the last 2-3 months. The key question therefore is it time to buy the shares now? Saha’s appointment is expected to ensure strategic continuity, develop the bank’s retail lending portfolio further, and address some concerns around execution, pressure on net interest margins (NIM), and a decline in the current account savings account (CASA) ratio. Kotak Mahindra Bank: Succession overhang cleared “The appointment of Anup Saha removes an overhang over leadership succession and is a positive development,” said Dnyanada Vaidya, Research Analyst - BFSI at Axis Direct. The brokerage has been constructive on the stock from before the appointment due to the lender’s ability to deliver healthy growth, deliver healthy growth, strong liability franchise, steady asset quality, and consistent RoA delivery of over 2%, despite margin pressures. ALSO READ5 Stocks Where FIIs Increased Their Stakes in Q2FY27 Sameer Sawant, Research Analyst at Mirae Asset Sharekhan echoed a similar sentiment. Sawant said Saha’s appointment is a positive and largely expected development. Saha’s broad experience across banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and a "potentially long tenure” give him room to make decisive long-term changes. Kotak Mahindra Bank's Q2 business update Source: Kotak Mahindra Bank press release Kotak Mahindra Bank: Key constraints The key constraint to Kotak Mahindra Bank’s growth story remains funding, said Antu Eapen Thomas, Senior Research Analyst at Geojit Investments. Loan growth continues to outpace deposit mobilisation, which is leading to a decline in the CASA ratio and is creating pressure on the lender’s margins. Thomas said sustained improvement in deposit franchise and margin expansion will be critical for the bank to regain its historical valuation premium and drive further re-rating. Mirae Asset’s Sawant flagged execution as the key constraint currently. The bank has already outperformed peers, and the market will now closely watch how the new management delivers on its roadmap, especially on deposit growth and the retail growth strategy. Similarly, Axis’ Vaidya views pressure on NIMs as one of the constraints. “At present, growth is led by secured retail, SME (small and medium enterprise) and Corporate. Unsecured growth has been lagging given the bank's calibrated stance as it emerged through the unsecured downcycle. Resultantly, the bank has seen pressure on NIMs,” Vaidya said. A revival in unsecured growth should also provide fillip to the lender’s margins. “Furthermore, given the reversal of the rate cycle, we expect Kotak's margins to improve. Kotak continues to remain amongst our top picks in the banking space,” Vaidya added. ALSO READHDFC Bank down 29% this year: Is it a ‘Buy’ now as Anup Bagchi takes charge? Kotak Mahindra’s retail lending outlook A calibrated increase in retail lending is expected under Saha, with unsecured loans having the scope to rise towards the bank’s medium-term target of around 15% of advances from the current 8.8%, Geojit’s Thomas said. He added that mortgages, loans against property, and SME lending should remain key growth drivers. Thomas said on the liability side, the focus is likely to shift towards strengthening CASA through Kotak 811 and salary account acquisition rather than relying on higher-cost term deposits. Vaidya said Saha could ensure a further boost to the retail and unsecured portfolio as he leverages his previous experiences at Bajaj Finance and ICICI Bank. Axis’ Vaidya said they will also watch out for Saha’s strategy of deposit mobilisation and leveraging the 811 platform. Mirae’s Sawant said, “We expect the bank to stay focused on retail and consumer banking, with disciplined capital deployment and deposit mobilisation underpinning growth, while keeping a careful stance on unsecured credit.” Kotak Mahindra Bank: Renewed focus and retail growth The appointment of Anup Saha as MD, CEO has removed the uncertainties around leadership succession. Now, analysts expect more focus on growing the retail portfolio, leveraging the 811 platform, and improving margins. Disclaimer: This article provides factual analysis only and is not, and should not be construed as, an offer, solicitation, or recommendation to buy or sell securities. Investors must conduct their own independent due diligence and seek advice from a SEBI-registered financial advisor.

docs.title: Mr President, now you understand India
docs.text: Last week, President Donald Trump made a bold pivot that reshaped the global energy debate. Faced with high diesel prices at home, weeks before the US mid-term elections, he turned to President Vladimir Putin. Russia agreed to supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately to the American and global markets, with supplies rising to one million tonnes by December. President Trump explained his objective with characteristic clarity: bring down prices for American farmers, ranchers, truckers, and consumers. That decision reflects the same practical logic India has consistently followed in securing affordable energy. ALSO READMechanical tightening could unnecessarily damage growth Mr President, I hope now you understand India’s compulsion. The Lindsey O. Graham Act of 2026 empowers the US President to impose tariffs of up to 100% on major purchasers of Russian energy. But what matters is how fairly he exercises his discretion. India’s case has always been straightforward. We are one of the world’s largest importers of crude oil. Energy is not a discretionary purchase for us. Its price flows through almost everything an Indian household consumes. India bought Russian crude for its competitive price. Much has changed since then. And those changes have strengthened India’s argument. Saudi Arabia has sharply reduced crude prices for Asian buyers. Venezuelan crude has become increasingly attractive to Indian refiners because of deep discounts, while Russian crude has become relatively more expensive. India swiftly diversified its crude sources. That matters because it establishes something often lost in the geopolitical debate. India’s policy was never: we must buy Russian oil. It was: we must buy affordable energy. If you want India to buy less Russian oil, make alternative oil competitive. Markets can often accomplish what sanctions and threats cannot. Then came the US’s own encounter with the same reality. President Trump turned to Russian diesel because American consumers were hurting. There’s nothing inherently wrong with that. An elected government is expected to protect the economic interests of its people. But that principle cannot stop at US borders. In 2025, India’s GDP per capita stood at about $2,700, a fraction of America’s approximately $90,000. Yet when high diesel prices threaten American farmers and households, Washington considers it legitimate to relax restrictions and bring Russian diesel into the American and global markets. When India buys discounted Russian crude for 1.4 billion people, it is asked to absorb the higher cost of alternative energy—or risk economic consequences. Why is affordability a valid national interest in Washington, but a questionable foreign-policy goal for New Delhi? For millions of Indians, affordable energy isn’t just economics; it affects everyday life. A small rise in diesel prices ripples far beyond the fuel pump and eventually reaches almost every household. If fuel inflation is politically painful in one of the world’s richest countries, imagine its consequences in a country with barely 3% of America’s GDP per capita. What Washington once questioned as India’s justification has now, in substance, become Washington’s own policy. Even in 2025, Russia remained the European Union’s second-largest supplier of LNG. European governments have industries to protect, households to heat, and economies to run. Precisely the same understanding must extend to India. There is a larger lesson here. Countries may speak the language of principles, but governments have a fundamental responsibility to their own citizens. When energy security, economic stability, or national security is threatened, even the world’s most powerful nations preserve room for manoeuvre. India must preserve the same room for itself. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government deserves credit for resisting considerable international pressure when India’s energy security required it, without turning that resistance into an ideological alignment with Moscow. India has not picked Russia over America—or Ukraine. It has chosen India. If Saudi crude is cheaper and commercially appropriate, we should buy Saudi crude. If Venezuelan oil offers better economics and can lawfully be purchased, refiners should buy Venezuelan oil. And where Russian crude remains commercially compelling and lawful, the Indian government cannot reasonably be expected to make its citizens pay substantially more merely to satisfy another country’s geopolitical preference. ALSO READJio changed telecom, Starlink faces the test That is not alignment. It is strategic autonomy. And strategic autonomy matters increasingly in a world where economic and geopolitical power are again inseparable. India’s ability to maintain that autonomy also tells us something about national strength. A country needs sufficient economic weight, diplomatic credibility, and political leadership to secure a seat at the table. Without them, sooner or later, others begin making its choices for it. Ironically, we have arrived at a clearer understanding. America wanted India to understand why Russian energy presented a geopolitical problem. India wanted America to understand why affordable energy was an economic necessity. Perhaps today both understand each other a little better. President Trump’s decision to secure Russian diesel should not be condemned. It should be understood for what it is: a government acting to protect its people from higher energy costs. India seeks no special treatment—just the same understanding America gives itself. Mr President, if Russian diesel can help protect an American farmer or trucker from unaffordable fuel prices, surely you can understand why the world’s largest democracy cannot casually pass higher energy costs on to 1.4 billion Indians. Your citizens matter. So do ours. The writer is Founder & Managing Partner, Saraf & Partners Law Offices Disclaimer: The views expressed are the author's own and do not reflect

docs.title: From the US to Kenya: 6 Indian textile stocks expanding despite tariff uncertainty
docs.text: India's textile exporters are facing another round of uncertainty as trade negotiations between India and the United States have stalled once again. Despite a framework agreement reached in February 2026, the two countries have yet to finalise a trade deal. According to a Reuters report dated 6 October 2026, negotiations have reached a standstill, with uncertainty over future tariffs remaining unresolved. For India's textile industry, the stakes are high. The US is a major export destination for Indian garments and home textiles. Higher tariffs could make Indian products less competitive against suppliers from other countries. This could affect export orders, revenue growth and operating margins. Prolonged uncertainty could also make it harder for companies to plan production and investments. However, not all textile exporters face the same level of risk. Some companies depend heavily on American customers and manufacture primarily in India. Others have expanded their manufacturing operations across Africa, Southeast Asia and the Americas, offering some protection against India-specific tariffs. The key question is whether overseas manufacturing, geographical diversification and pricing power can help these businesses protect their profitability. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now To examine this, we shortlisted six listed textile exporters with substantial exposure to the US market. These companies differ in their business models, manufacturing locations and financial positions. Their ability to withstand tariff pressures could therefore vary significantly. Let's take a closer look at these six textile exporters and assess how well they are positioned to navigate the renewed trade uncertainty. #1 Gokaldas Exports: African Manufacturing Offers a Buffer Against US Tariffs Gokaldas Exports is a leading apparel exporter supplying global fashion brands. According to its FY26 annual report North America contributed 77.9% of FY26 sales, making US tariff uncertainty a significant concern. However, its manufacturing operations in Kenya and Ethiopia provide alternative sourcing options. The annual report further shows the company's African manufacturing presence offers greater flexibility in serving American customers. Its Kenyan operations benefit from preferential US market access under the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA). The company is also seeing increased sourcing interest from American and European buyers. Its expertise in high-value outerwear positions it to compete for additional orders as global brands reassess their sourcing strategies. Capacity Expansion Supports Growth, but Tariff Risks Remain Gokaldas is expanding manufacturing capacity in Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka. Its second Madhya Pradesh unit is expected to approach full utilisation by Q4 FY27. African facilities could also increase production through additional shifts. In FY26, consolidated revenue from operations rose 3.2% YoY to Rs 3,987.6 crore. However, net profit declined 36.8% to Rs 100.1 crore. US trade measures imposed an estimated Rs 97 crore in additional costs. The company has yet to declare Q2 FY27 results. Its August earnings call indicated that orders for the quarter were already secured. However, prolonged tariff uncertainty, rising freight costs and possible changes to African trade benefits could pressure margins despite geographical diversification. ALSO READ5 Stocks Where FIIs Increased Their Stakes in Q2FY27 Gokaldas Exports 1-Year Share Price Chart Source: Screener.in #2 Welspun Living: US Manufacturing Offers a Partial Hedge Against Tariff Pressures Welspun Living is a major home textile exporter supplying towels, bed linen and other products to global retailers. According to its FY26 annual report, the US accounted for approximately 59% of FY26 business, making the company particularly exposed to tariff uncertainty. However, its manufacturing facilities in Ohio and Nevada provide some protection against India-specific tariffs. The Nevada pillow facility commenced commercial production in FY26, while Ohio continues to scale operations. Management is targeting $60 million in US pillow revenue in FY27. Geographical Diversification and Modernisation Support Recovery The FY26 annual report also shows that non-US markets accounted for around 41% of business. The company is expanding its presence in the UK and Europe, supported by established retailer relationships and the India-UK trade agreement. Welspun has also approved a Rs 121 crore modernisation project at Anjar to improve manufacturing efficiency. In FY26, consolidated revenue declined 10.9% YoY to Rs 9,399.1 crore, while net profit fell 68% to Rs 204.4 crore. US tariffs affected demand, pricing and shipment volumes. The company has yet to declare Q2 FY27 results. Its August earnings call indicated that flooding at the Vapi facility could disrupt Q2 operations, with recovery expected in subsequent quarters. Despite overseas manufacturing and diversification, Indian towel and bed-linen exports remain vulnerable to prolonged tariff uncertainty. docs.title: Defending the rupee
docs.text:
Sign In 
 CLOSE 
 For uninterrupted reading, switch to App
 READ IN APP 
 Written by The Financial Express 
 Updated: October 13, 2026 07:38 IST 
 Follow Us 
 Unable to arrest the rupee ‘s depreciation through currency-market interventions, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has moved to curb dollar demand and speculation. It has tightened rules governing foreign exchange derivatives: contracts cannot be cancelled and rebooked, positions exceeding $5 million must have an underlying exposure, and banks must set aside 20% of the value of contracts exceeding $2 million in cash. Banks must also ensure that the same exposure is not hedged through multiple dealers. Together with a special dollar window for state-owned oil marketing companies, these constitute perhaps the strongest defence of the currency since 2013. Despite its assertions that it does not defend the rupee at any particular level, the RBI’s latest moves suggest that a sharp depreciation is unacceptable. The dollar’s approach towards `97 appears to have prompted the intervention, making that level a possible line in the sand.
At last Wednesday’s post-monetary policy press conference, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra maintained that the rupee was not overvalued, citing the real effective exchange rate, and observed that markets could be “irrational” in the short run. However, the central bank’s efforts to stem the slide have been undermined by rising US Treasury yields, elevated oil prices, and foreign portfolio outflows. The rupee’s fall to 96.73 against the dollar last Friday, close to its record low of 96.82, appears to have triggered the latest measures. The over 40% surge in Brent crude since the start of the Iran war, accompanied by a roughly 5% depreciation of the rupee, has compounded India’s external vulnerabilities. A weaker currency raises the import bill and fuels inflation, particularly with crude above $100 a barrel and uncertainty over Russian oil supplies. This could force the RBI to tighten monetary policy more aggressively, eventually hurting credit growth.
The restrictions should deter speculation and make it harder to circumvent hedging rules. Importers will face tighter requirements for hedging current-account exposures, although the restrictions do not apply to foreign portfolio investors. Hedging costs, estimated to rise by 80-150 basis points from the prevailing 3.5%, should discourage excessive derivative positions. The special dollar window for oil marketing companies should also reduce demand in the spot market. Earlier this year, the RBI capped banks’ daily net open rupee positions at $100 million and restricted their participation in rupee non-deliverable forwards. Clearly, with the global environment turning adverse, the central bank is unwilling to risk another disorderly depreciation. Although foreign currency reserves have reportedly been bolstered by $142 billion in foreign currency non-resident ( bank ) deposits and foreign currency borrowings, sustained dollar sales could quickly erode these buffers without necessarily reversing the rupee’s trajectory.
The rupee sprang back to an intra-day high of 95.77 against the dollar on Monday, suggesting the measures have had the desired immediate impact. But administrative restrictions and market interventions can only buy time. Elevated oil prices, a strong dollar and persistent capital outflows will continue to weigh on the currency.Unless the global environment improves and India’s trade deficit narrows, the rupee will remain vulnerable to renewed selling. Some fiscal measures, including higher retail fuel prices to contain demand, may become necessary. Further monetary tightening to anchor inflation expectations and measures to attract durable capital inflows may also be required. The RBI has demonstrated its determination to prevent a sharp slide in the rupee. Sustaining that defence, however, will depend as much on developments beyond India’s borders as on its own policy actions.

docs.title: Divi’s to Sai Life: Jefferies outlines 4 CRDMO stocks positioned to capture global orders
docs.text: Choosing a winner among India’s drug-making service providers is a bit like picking a restaurant when every menu looks similar. Financial performance forecasts often look alike, so investors need another way to tell the companies apart. In the Jefferies report dated October 12, 2026, four names deserve a close look. This includes Divi’s Laboratories, Sai Life Sciences, Laurus Labs and Anthem Biosciences. Out of these, Divi’s and Sai Life lead on the factors the report treats as most important for long-term growth. As per the global investment bank Jefferies report, investors need to understand what drives a company’s growth. Some of the factors include its relationships with global pharmaceutical companies, manufacturing capabilities, research pipeline and ability to deliver projects reliably. Let's take a look at what the report says - Pharma sector: What is a CRDMO? In simple words, a Contract Research, Development and Manufacturing Organisation (CRDMO) works for global drug companies. It helps invent a medicine, tests it and then makes it in bulk. In the recent years, India’s sector has seen a revival with Sai Life, Anthem Biosciences, Cohance and Piramal Pharma all arriving on the stock market. ALSO READIndia’s telecom equipment market could double to $50 Bn: 3 stocks making 5G gear Jefferies argues that financial forecasts are only the outcome of deeper business strengths. The report noted, "a key challenge for investors remains differentiating these companies beyond financial performance." Divi’s Laboratories and Sai Life Sciences: Big Pharma relationships matter Relationships with large global pharmaceutical companies could be an important source of future growth for Indian CRDMOs. According to Jefferies report, "We believe the ongoing geographic diversification trend is largely driven by global pharmaceutical companies. Consequently, firms with deeper Big Pharma relationships are likely to outgrow peers." The global investment bank report identifies Divi’s Laboratories and Sai Life Sciences as the strongest among the companies assessed on this parameter. Such relationships can help CRDMOs gain access to new projects and build business over the long term, although actual growth will depend on project wins and execution. Sai Life and Anthem Biosciences: Manufacturing capabilities in focus The ability to support a drug from its early research stage through large-scale manufacturing is another factor investors should track. Pharmaceutical companies may prefer partners that can handle multiple stages of a drug’s development, reducing the need to work with several service providers. According to Jefferies, “We view Sai Life as the most integrated Indian CRDMO, followed by Anthem Bio.” The report also highlighted the importance of contract development and manufacturing organisation (CDMO) services compared with contract research organisation (CRO) services. Manufacturing contracts can provide more consistent revenue once products enter commercial production, although the timing and scale of commercialisation remain important. Anthem Biosciences: Specialised research and manufacturing Expertise in newer and more complex drug technologies could help companies differentiate themselves in an increasingly competitive market. Biologics, peptides and oligonucleotides require specialised research and manufacturing capabilities and can offer opportunities to serve pharmaceutical companies developing advanced treatments. Jefferies believes Anthem Biosciences has some of the strongest manufacturing capabilities in these areas. These technologies can generate higher revenue per molecule, according to the Jefferies report, while potentially supporting business over several years. However, the commercial opportunity depends on successful project development and customer demand. ALSO READHCLTech jumps 5%: Nomura sees 9% upside but Nuvama warns of unfavourable risk-reward Divi’s and Laurus Labs: Project pipeline and manufacturing scale A CRDMO’s future growth also depends on the nature of the projects it secures. Projects involving large patient populations, high drug volumes and complex molecules can provide greater revenue opportunities. Jefferies highlighted Divi’s Laboratories and Laurus Labs for their exposure to peptides, while Sai Life Sciences and Anthem Biosciences have healthy pipelines of small-molecule projects. Manufacturing capacity is another consideration. Large pharmaceutical customers may require dedicated production facilities, significant investment and sufficient technical staff from their partners. According to Jefferies, “We believe Divi's and Laurus offer among the strongest large-scale manufacturing capabilities.” Execution remains critical for all four stocks Beyond capacity and research expertise, companies must deliver projects on time, maintain product quality and comply with regulatory requirements. Delays or quality issues can affect customer relationships and future business opportunities. Jefferies noted that operational indicators are not always publicly available, making management quality and past performance useful measures for investors. The firm identifies Divi’s Laboratories, Laurus Labs, Anthem Biosciences and Sai Life Sciences as companies that stand out on execution. The views, target prices, and recommendations expressed are those of the respective brokerage firms and do not reflect the official policy or position of Financial Express. docs.title: Rs 34,200 cr Kavach opportunity: 2 railway safety stocks to watch as India upgrades its network
docs.text: India’s railway safety upgrade could create a sizeable opportunity for companies working on Kavach. The addressable broad-gauge network alone spans 81,000 route kilometres, representing an estimated ₹34,200 crore opportunity. Another 3,300 route kilometres lie across Dedicated Freight Corridors. But the rollout is far from over. Indian Railways plans to tender Kavach installation across another 41,000 route kilometres between FY27 and FY29. Demand also extends to new locomotives, with regulations requiring every newly manufactured locomotive to be equipped with Kavach before commissioning. With Indian Railways adding around five locomotives a day, or more than 1,900 a year, this requirement adds another source of demand for Kavach suppliers. Against this backdrop, this article examines two specialised players in rail-technology and safety equipment. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now #1 Kernex Microsystems: Riding India’s Kavach Revolution Kernex Microsystems is a rail-technology and safety systems company. The company designs, develops, and executes safety-critical railway electronics, signalling, and turnkey infrastructure projects. In turnkey projects, it delivers complete project lifecycle execution, from survey and design to installation. RDSO SIL-4 Certification Drives High-Volume Kavach Rollout The company can produce 6,000 Loco Kavach units, 1,000 Station Kavach units, 500 Remote Interface Units, and 120 Level Crossing Gates (scalable to 300) annually. Kernex is the first OEM to commercially operate Kavach on Vande Bharat trainsets and the first to interface with four different Electronic Interlocking systems. ₹5,174-Crore Order Book Locks in Visible Revenue Through FY29 Kernex holds a total Kavach contract portfolio of ₹5,174 crore (inclusive of GST). To date, ₹1,687 crore (33%) has been executed, leaving a balance order book of ₹3,487 crore (67%). For the FY27-29 horizon, Kernex's cumulative executable base builds to ₹6,727 crore. This comprises ₹2,105 crore projected for FY27, ₹2,200 crore for FY28, and ₹2,422 crore for FY29. An additional ₹2,420 crore from these contract awards is projected to be executed from FY30 onwards. The executable base highlights the monetary value of work scheduled to be executed into revenue over a given financial period. Kernex holds RDSO approval for Kavach Version 4.0 under SIL 4 safety standards, placing it within a limited set of certified suppliers. Post-Commissioning AMCs: The 37x Recurring Cash Flow Engine Kavach deployment also offers a multi-decadal recurring income opportunity. Beyond the initial equipment installation, long-term revenue streams are generated through software upgrades, hardware modifications, and Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs). Management projects the AMC revenues alone to grow from ₹5 crore in FY27 to ₹185 crore in FY29. Non-Rail Diversification and ₹150-Crore Global Pipeline Take Shape To expand beyond the core business of railway signalling, Kernex is diversifying into adjacent critical-infrastructure sectors. These comprise Yard Management Systems, Intelligent Traffic Management, Data Centres & Disaster Recovery, and Simulators. Internationally, the company is targeting a ₹150 crore export opportunity over the next two years. ALSO READSunil Singhania’s Rs 266 cr bet, Madhu Kela’s 20x order-book play – stocks up 100%+ Q1 Operating Margins Expand to 32.3% as Operating Leverage Kicks In Financially, consolidated revenue surged to ₹504 crore in Q1FY27, up from ₹56 crore in Q1FY26. EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation, and Amortisation) rose to ₹163 crore from ₹10 crore in Q1FY26, while margin stood at 32.3%. Net profit surged to ₹110 crore, up from ₹7 crore in Q1FY26. Order book execution remains the key going ahead. Q1FY27 earnings are yet to be announced. Kernex Share Price #2 Concord Control Systems: Beyond Kavach, Building the Future of Rail Safety Concord Control Systems is a railway technology platform company. It develops mission-critical electronics, safety systems, propulsion technologies, and diagnostic solutions. It is an approved OEM and vendor for Indian Railways bodies, including the RDSO, Chittaranjan Locomotive Works, and Integral Coach Factory. RDSO Vendor Status and Vertical Supply Chain Integration Concord participates in the Kavach program through Progota, in which it holds a 46.5% stake. It operates as an indigenous R&D player developing proprietary technology in-house. Through its backward integration with Fusion Electronics (PCBs and box-build solutions) and Advanced Rail Controls, it benefits from cost efficiencies and vertical integration for its Kavach hardware. Concord's Kavach suite includes both onboard locomotive hardware and control infrastructure. Concord secured ₹258.3 crore in total Kavach orders during FY26. This includes major contract wins of ₹185.1 crore and ₹53.7 crore for on-board Kavach 4.0 equipment. The execution timeline is 12 months. ₹697-Crore Order Book Underpins 3.3x Revenue Visibility Concord closed FY26 with an executable order book of ₹697 crore, up 228% year-on-year. This order provides 3.3x revenue visibility relative to FY26 revenue of ₹210 crore. Following its 80% acquisition, Fusion Electronics is expected to become a direct revenue contributor in FY27. The Kavach platform yields 25-30% EBITDA margins and generates long-term recurring revenue through 15-year maintenance contracts. Looking ahead, management is guiding for a 40% to 50% revenue CAGR over the coming years. Management maintains a sustainable baseline target of 22% to 25% EBITDA margins. Expanding Into 15-Year Maintenance and Digital Signalling Assets By FY30, management aims to shift a significant portion of its revenue from one-off equipment manufacturing to high-margin, annuity-based streams. This includes AMCs, software licenses, diagnostics analytics, and IP royalties

docs.title: Steel prices climb to 4-year highs: Why Nomura is bullish on Tata Steel, JSW Steel
docs.text: Steel prices in India have climbed to near four-year highs, and costs for key raw materials have started to ease. Hot-rolled coil (HRC), a flat steel used in construction, autos and pipes, rose Rs 700 a tonne in the week ended October 9 to Rs 64,700, as per a Nomura report. Rebar, the steel bars used in buildings, gained Rs 900 to Rs 63,800 a tonne. Three factors are supporting the sector, and the brokerage has kept its Buy rating on Tata Steel, JSW Steel and Jindal Steel, the report noted. Steel prices and mill margins rise The first driver is the rise in steel prices. Rebar has recovered after a soft patch that began in the April-June quarter. The price gap between flat and long steel has narrowed to about Rs 900 a tonne, the report noted. The profit mills earn on each tonne of HRC has improved as well. It stands at about Rs 39,110 a tonne this month, up roughly Rs 3,000 from the July-September quarter, as per the report. Indian steel is also priced above Chinese imports. Chinese HRC costs about Rs 61,953 a tonne once it reaches an Indian port, so domestic prices are about 4% higher. Steel from Japan and Korea costs Rs 68,452 a tonne at the port, which is about 5% above Indian prices, the report noted. Nomura expects the price increases to cover any rise in raw material costs. It sees mills benefiting in the first half of FY27, as per the report. ALSO READFM invites global steel body to set up India office Coking coal and iron ore prices ease The second driver is a pause in input cost increases. Imported coking coal, which is used to make steel in blast furnaces, fell $3 a tonne during the week to $271. That is about 3% below the September average, as per the report. Coking coal had risen sharply earlier because of supply problems at key producers, geopolitical tensions and a fatal mine accident in China. Chinese spot prices have eased by $6 to $352 a tonne but remain more than 40% above their level before the accident, the report noted. Iron ore has weakened too. The global benchmark fell to $87 a tonne, its lowest level this year. NMDC raised the price of lump ore by Rs 150 to Rs 5,400 a tonne from September, while fines, a grade of ore, stayed at Rs 4,500, as per the report. China remains a point to watch. Its export HRC price was steady at $510 a tonne, and its mills earned margins of $130 a tonne on domestic sales. Nomura described Chinese export margins as close to their lowest levels and said a recovery looked unlikely, the report noted. National Steel Policy targets 604 MT capacity by 2047 The third driver is the draft National Steel Policy, which replaces the 2017 framework. It aims to raise India's crude steel capacity to 604 million tonnes by 2047 from about 220 million tonnes now, as per the Nomura report. Crude steel production rose from about 89 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 170 million tonnes in 2025-26. Finished steel consumption climbed from 77 million tonnes to 164 million tonnes over the same period, as per the draft policy. Demand is expected to reach 505 million tonnes by 2047. Steel use per person is projected to rise to 302 kg from 116 kg in FY26. The global average is 209 kg, the draft noted. Construction and infrastructure account for about 67% of steel use at present. The draft expects manufacturing to add to demand, in areas such as autos, capital goods and renewable energy equipment. It assumes the economy will grow about 7% a year over the long term, as per the draft policy. ALSO READ7.6% growth, best-ever Q2 auto volumes: Tata Steel’s India expansion pays off India is already shifting on trade. It became a net exporter of finished steel in 2025-26. Imports fell about 32% to 6.5 million tonnes, while exports rose about 36% to 6.6 million tonnes. The draft sets a target of 45 million tonnes of exports by 2047, the draft noted. Coking coal imports and steel emissions remain challenges Securing raw materials is a major focus. They make up 65 to 70% of the cost of making steel, as per the draft policy. India will need 772 million tonnes of iron ore and 236 million tonnes of coking coal by 2047. Coking coal demand was 72 million tonnes in 2025-26, the draft noted. India is largely self-sufficient in iron ore but imports nearly 92% of its coking coal, mainly from Australia, the US and Russia. This leaves steelmakers exposed to global price swings, as per the report. The draft also points to a gap at home. Coal washing capacity stands at about 39 million tonnes a year, but actual output is only about 6 million tonnes because of low yields and idle capacity, the draft noted. The policy proposes more domestic mining, more coal washeries and the purchase of overseas mines. It also suggests long-term supply deals and the use of artificial intelligence to improve coal blending, as per the Nomura report. Emissions are another pressure point. Steel accounts for 10 to 12% of India's carbon dioxide emissions. The sector emits 2.54 tonnes of carbon dioxide for every tonne of crude steel, against a global average of about 1.92 tonnes. The draft aims to bring this down to 1.54 tonnes by 2047, as per the draft policy. Tata Steel, JSW Steel share price targets Nomura expects the large Indian steelmakers to earn more per tonne than they have in a typical business cycle over FY27 to FY29. Tata Steel is expected to earn the most per tonne among the three, the report noted. Tata Steel trades at a 13% discount to its three-year average valuation, while Jindal Steel is at a 2% discount. JSW Steel is close to its average, as per the report. The brokerage's target prices are Rs 240 for Tata Steel, Rs 1,400 for JSW Steel and Rs 1,300 for Jindal Steel. Risks include weak Chinese margins, higher Chinese exports, project delays and slower domestic demand, as per the report.

docs.title: Welspun Corp to JSW Steel: Jefferies’ top metal picks for Q2
docs.text: India’s metal and mining companies are expected to post good numbers for the second quarter of financial year 2027 (Q2FY27). Global investment bank Jefferies has chosen Welspun Corp. and JSW Steel as its preferred picks amongst metal stocks for the quarter. Jefferies on Welspun Corp: To benefit from multi-year upcycle The investment bank said Welspun Corp is well positioned to benefit from a multi-year upcycle in oil & gas infrastructure spending in the US and Middle East, which is supported by local manufacturing in both the regions. The company is expected to deliver its sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit EBITDA growth, with Q2FY27 EBITDA seen rising 19% year-on-year. Strong order execution in the US will more than offset weakness in India. Welspun Corp’s pipe sales volumes are expected to fall 16% due to continued weakness in India. ALSO READRs 2.35 lakh cr naval push: 2 stocks to watch as India targets 200 warships Jefferies on JSW Steel: HRC prices in focus Jefferies remains constructive on JSW Steel, as hot rolled coil (HRC) spot prices in India are currently 9% above their average for the September quarter. It expects further upside if Asian steel spreads mean revert, supporting a stronger earnings outlook. JSW Steel’s consolidated volumes for the quarter are expected to rise 8-10% YoY. The company’s EBITDA per tonne is seen declining 8-9% sequentially, primarily due to higher costs. However, higher volumes should partly offset margin pressure, with consolidated EBITDA seen rising 5% sequentially. Jefferies on other metal players: Hindustan Zinc, Hindalco, Coal India, among others Volumes Volume growth in the sector will be led by Shyam Metalics and Energy, with 21% YoY growth, according to Jefferies. Tata Steel’s volumes are also expected to rise 8-10%, while Coal India reported a 12% increase. Jefferies expect Jindal Stainless’ sales to rise a modest 3% YoY, reflecting production disruptions early in the quarter. It also sees Hindalco’s India aluminium sales to remain flat YoY and Novelis' volumes to grow just 1% YoY. Margins Tata Steel’s standalone EBITDA per tonne is expected to decline 8-9% sequentially, with consolidated EBITDA estimated to rise 9%. Jindal Stainless’ EBITDA is projected to recover 9% sequentially from the production constrained June quarter. Prices Hindustan Zinc’s EBITDA is expected to rise 7% sequentially, mainly due to higher zinc prices and strong growth in silver volumes. Jefferies expects Hindalco’s consolidated EBITDA to fall 17% QoQ but rise 29% YoY, led by a 15% QoQ fall in India aluminum EBITDA per tonne due to lower aluminum prices. It also expects Novelis' adjusted EBITDA per tonne to decline 9% QoQ to $511. ALSO READTata Steel to Jindal Steel: Key stocks poised to gain as domestic steel prices surge up to 24% Jefferies on metals and mining The global investment bank remains positive on the sector as volume growth is expected to drive earnings in Q2FY27. Jefferies prefers Welspun Corp as it sees a huge opportunity from the growing investment in oil and gas infra in the US and Middle East. It prefers JSW Steel because of rising HRC prices. The views, target prices, and recommendations expressed are those of the respective brokerage firms and do not reflect the official policy or position of Financial Express. Investors must conduct their own independent due diligence and seek advice from a SEBI-registered financial advisor before making any investment decisions.

docs.title: Dividend, rights issue record date: Last chance to buy today - Shivam Autotech, Shraddha Prime, Anand Rathi Wealth
docs.text:
Shivam Autotech has announced a rights issue and fixed October 15 as the record date, while Shraddha Prime Projects has also fixed the same date for its rights issue. Anand Rathi Wealth has fixed Thursday, October 15, as the record date to determine shareholder eligibility for its ₹ 4 interim dividend. Investors looking to benefit from this payout must ensure they own the stock before the record date. Under India’s T+1 settlement cycle, shares purchased on or after the record date will not qualify for the dividend. Shivam Autotech Limited has approved a rights issue of up to 10,000,000 fully paid-up equity shares, with a face value of ₹ 2 each, to raise up to ₹ 12,000 lakh ( ₹ 120 crore). The shares are priced at ₹ 12 per equity share, including a premium of ₹ 10 per share, with the full amount payable upon application. Eligible shareholders as of the record date, Thursday, October 15, 2026, will be offered 19 rights equity shares for every 25 fully paid-up equity shares held. The company said in its regulatory filing said, “The designated date for determining the equity shareholders who would be eligible to apply for the rights equity shares in the issue, subject to the terms and conditions set out in the issue materials, to be decided prior to the filing of this Letter of Offer, is Thursday, October 15, 2026.” Shraddha Prime Projects has also approved a rights issue worth ₹ 96.96 crore, through which the company will issue 60.60 lakh equity shares at ₹ 160 apiece, including a premium of ₹ 150 per share. The rights issue will offer three new shares for every 20 shares held by eligible shareholders. Investors will need to pay ₹ 144 per share on application, with the remaining ₹ 16 payable on a subsequent call. The record date to determine shareholder eligibility has been fixed for October 15, 2026. The company has also appointed GYR Capital Advisors Private Limited as the merchant banker for the issue. Along with its September-quarter results, Anand Rathi Wealth declared an interim dividend of ₹ 4 per equity share and fixed October 15 as the record date. The company posted a 22% increase in consolidated net profit to ₹ 122 crore for the September quarter of FY27, driven by revenue growth. Its revenue from operations rose 16% to ₹ 356.6 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with ₹ 307 crore a year ago, the company said in a statement. Anand Rathi Wealth’s assets under management (AUM) rose 18% year-on-year to ₹ 108,377 crore as of September 30, 2026. Disclaimer : We advise investors to check with certified experts before making any investment decisions. Ksheera Sagar has been working as a Market Research Analyst at LiveMint for the past four years, covering stocks, commodities, and broader financial markets. In this role, he closely tracks daily market movements, corporate earnings, sector trends, and macroeconomic developments.

He has over a decade of experience in the financial services industry and has previously worked with multiple organisations, including global investment bank J.P. Morgan, bringing strong research experience into the newsroom.

During his career, he has gained extensive exposure to equity research, market analysis, and financial data interpretation, strengthening his expertise across asset classes and market cycles.

He is known for his data-driven analysis and crisp, listicle-style market stories that break down complex financial developments across key markets for a wide audience. His strong research skills enable him to write detailed and insightful stories on stocks and sectors, focusing on the underlying factors driving market movements.

His work combines quantitative insights with clear storytelling, presenting financial developments in a clear and structured manner. Moreover, he enjoys writing multibagger and listicle-style copies. Outside of work, Ksheera enjoys playing the piano and exploring new places. He has a keen interest in travel, music, and continuously learning about global markets and economic trends.  Stocks to buy today: Kotak Neo's Shrikant Chouhan has shared a bullish view on Bharat Electronics Limited and Greenply Industries Limited.
 Kotak Neo's Shrikant Chouhan bullish on BEL, Greenply; check targets
 Shrikant Chouhan Mumbai 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 13 2026 | 7:38 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion. 
 Stocks to buy recommendations by Shrikant Chouhan, Head of Equity Research, Kotak Neo 
 Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL): Add 
 CMP: ₹374 
 FV: ₹410 
 Stock Market LIVE: Sensex gains nearly 600 pts, Nifty tops 22,500; VIX drops 5%
 Maruti Suzuki tanks 33% in calendar year 2026; stock hits 18-month low

 Resistance: ₹383, ₹390 
 Support: ₹366, ₹360 
 Bharat Electronics Ltd (BEL) is well positioned to sustain its growth momentum, supported by a strong pipeline of large defence programs, including QRSAM, AMCA and key naval projects such as P75I and NGC. Management expects the year-end order book to exceed Rs1 lakh cr, compared with approximately ₹75,000 crore, which remained broadly flat over the past three years. The anticipated increase will be driven by a healthy pipeline of base orders exceeding ₹25,000 crore and the ₹30,000 crore QRSAM program, significantly strengthening revenue visibility.
 Missiles are emerging as BEL’s second-largest growth vertical after electronics, supported by its participation in key programs such as QRSAM, Pralay, Nirbhay/LRLACM and Project Kusha. Missile revenues are expected to scale up to a high-double-digit share of overall revenues over the next 2–3 years. The approximately ₹30,000 crore QRSAM program remains the most important near-term growth catalyst. Under Project Kusha, India’s indigenous long-range air-defence initiative, BEL is keen to be selected by DRDO as the lead integrator, with BDL manufacturing the missiles.
 In the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) program, BEL is among the three shortlisted consortia following technical evaluation. The company remains hopeful of emerging as the L1 bidder alongside L&T, with an equal work-share arrangement already locked in, offering potential long-term growth opportunities.
 Operationally, BEL has delivered a strong 17 per cent revenue CAGR over FY24–FY26 and continues to guide for revenue growth of over 15 per cent in the medium term. Ebitda margins have expanded to nearly 30 per cent, supported by higher indigenization, operating leverage and a favourable product mix. The expected improvement in order inflows should provide strong revenue visibility over the next 3–4 years.
 Healthy order prospects, improving business mix and sustained visibility on India’s defence spending underpin our constructive outlook on BEL. We maintain our Add rating with a fair value of ₹410, based on an unchanged valuation multiple of 33x September 2028E earnings. Check - TOP GAINERS NSE | TOP LOSERS NSE 
 Greenply Industries Limited (Greenply): Buy 
 CMP: ₹314 
 FV: ₹354 
 Resistance: ₹325, ₹335 
 Support: ₹305, ₹295 
 Greenply Industries Limited (Greenply) business segments include wood based products including plywood and MDF (medium density fiberboard). In the plywood segment, the management has guided 10 per cent volume growth in FY27E. In Q1FY27, plywood volume grew by 13.8 per cent Y-o-Y. Greenply’s plywood volume growth is expected to benefit from BIS implementation, lower imports, investment in ECOTEC brand and internal process improvement. For plywood margins, the management is positive that operating leverage benefits will come into play with higher revenue. We believe that the plywood segment Ebitda margins have scope for improvement, led by operational efficiency and process improvement at its plant. MDF segment is expected to support revenue growth as the company expanded capacity in FY26 and another line is being added. The management has guided 25-30 per cent MDF volume growth in FY27E. MDF volumes grew by 24.7 per cent Y-o-Y in Q1FY27. The company is focusing on selling value added products and that along with improved efficiencies and operating leverage from high volumes is expected to support Ebitda margin in the MDF segment. Further, any correction in timber prices would be an added advantage. The company has taken price hikes in both the timber and the MDF segment in Q1FY27, to pass on the increase in chemical prices and higher logistics cost (in imports). In the plywood segment, the company is constructing a new plant in Odisha with an outlay of ₹130 crore and expanding MDF capacity, that entails an investment of ₹425 crore. We expect the earnings growth momentum to continue in FY27E and FY28E. We have a Buy rating and a fair value of ₹354 on the stock. docs.title: Buy ICICI Prudential AMC Ltd for the Target Rs 3,700 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Strong revenue growth drives an all-round beat 
* ICICI Prudential AMC’s (IPRU) operating revenue grew 18% YoY/7% QoQ to INR16.7b (7% beat) in 2QFY27. Yields came in at 57.9bp vs. 56bp in 2QFY26 and 56.1bp in 1QFY27. Operating net revenue mix stood at 89.9% for mutual funds, 8.7% for alternates and 1.4% for advisory.
* Total opex at INR4.6b was up 23% YoY/6% QoQ. Employee costs at INR2b rose 23% YoY/4% QoQ, while other expenses came in at INR1.1b, up 14% YoY/9% QoQ. EBIDTA came in at INR12.2b (9% beat), up 16% YoY and 7% QoQ. EBIDTA margin was at 72.6% vs. 73.8% in 2QFY26 and 72.4% in 1QFY27.
* PAT stood at INR8.9b (13% beat mainly due to higher revenue growth), up 6% YoY but down 8% QoQ. PAT margins came in at 53.1% vs. 58.8% in 2QFY26 and 61.7% in 1QFY27.
* The company has launched NFOs across a balanced hybrid fund, multi-asset active FoF, dynamic asset allocation passive FoF, BSE Insurance ETF, and lifecycle funds with 5, 10 and 15-year maturities. On the SIF front, four funds have been launched, with a fifth planned for 2QFY27. Economics for SIFs are expected to remain broadly in line with MF business.
* We have raised our earnings estimates for FY27/FY28 by 4%/2%, factoring in higher other income and improved yields in the MF business, partially offset by a marginal increase in operating expenses. We project a CAGR of 16%/15%/15% in AUM/revenue/PAT over FY26-28E and maintain a BUY rating with a TP of INR3,700, based on 45x FY28E core EPS.
* Total MF QAAUM at INR11.6t grew 14% YoY and 4% QoQ. Equity/Hybrid/ETFs/Index/Liquid segments grew 14%/18%/41%/14%/12% YoY, but debt declined by 12% YoY in 2QFY27.
* The share of Equity/ETF/Debt/Liquid in the total QAUM stood at ~60%/ 13%/11%/11% in 2QFY27 vs. 59%/11%/15%/11% in 2QFY26.
* Alternates QAAUM grew 2% QoQ to INR810b, driven by PMS (INR308b; +6% QoQ) and AIF (INR243b; +7% QoQ), partly offset by a 6% QoQ decline in assets under advisory (INR259b). Yields improved sequentially due to drawdowns in certain funds, particularly real estate; historical yields have generally ranged around 90-100bp, with AIF/PMS yields at 97.2bp (vs. 95.2bp in 1QFY27) and Advisory yields at 33.7bp (vs. 29.9bp).
* Monthly systematic transactions (SIPs and STPs) moderated to INR46.7b in Sep’26 from INR48.7b in Jun’26 amid market volatility (in line with industry trends). Average SIP contribution remained broadly stable QoQ, while flows shifted toward small- and mid-cap schemes.
* Quarterly average SIF AUM increased to INR49.5b in 2QFY27 from INR26.8b in 1QFY27. Four SIF funds have been launched, with a fifth planned for 2QFY27. SIF margins and operating economics are expected to be broadly similar to the MF business.
* On the NFO front, the company launched products across multiple categories, including a balanced hybrid fund, multi-asset active FoF, dynamic asset allocation passive FoF, BSE Insurance ETF, and lifecycle funds with 5-, 10- and 15-year maturities.
* On the distribution front, MFDs remained dominant in the equity AUM mix at 36.1%, followed by direct at 29.9%, national distributors at 15.9%, and banks at ~18.1% in 2QFY27 vs. 36.2%/29.5%/15.9%/18.4% in 1QFY27, respectively.
* Unique customer base grew 3% QoQ to 17.8m as of Sep’26.
* The total investment book stood at INR51.9b as of Sep’26, with 77.8% in MFs (33.4% equity, 66.1% liquid & debt, balance others), 19.4% in AIF/other equity/REITs, and the remainder in corporate bonds (vs. 72.9% in MFs and 23.5% in AIF/other equity/REITs as of Jun’26).
* Total opex at INR4.6b was up 23% YoY/6% QoQ. Employee costs at INR2b rose 23% YoY/4% QoQ, while other expenses came in at INR1.1b, up 14% YoY/9% QoQ. As bp of AUM, opex was at 15.9bp vs. 14.7bp in 2QFY26 and 15.5bp in 1QFY27.
* FY27 ESOP expense guidance is reiterated at INR640-680m, with charges recognized in the P&L on a pro-rata basis.
* Fees and commission expenses increased 30% YoY, reflecting higher distribution payouts in the fast-growing AIF and PMS businesses.
* Other income came in at INR169m vs. our est. of negative INR350m.
* PAT increased 6.1% YoY to INR8.9b but declined 7.8% QoQ, primarily due to lower other income from mark-to-market movements.
* IPRU AMC remains well-positioned to deliver healthy growth, supported by strong net flows, product diversification and expansion in alternatives, including SIFs.
* We have raised our earnings estimates for FY27/FY28 by 4%/2%, factoring in higher other income and improved yields in the MF business, partially offset by a marginal increase in operating expenses. We project AUM/revenue/PAT CAGRs of 16%/15%/15% over FY26-FY28E and maintain a BUY rating with a TP of INR 3,700, based on 45x FY28E core EPS.

docs.title: Buy Billionbrains Garage Ventures Ltd for the Target Rs 240 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Volume cycle turning, new businesses building up 
* The regulatory overhang is easing, and Groww is well placed to gain. Broker and exchange stocks have corrected because options volumes dropped after two regulations took effect: the RBI's curbs on bank funding to prop traders (effective Jul'26) and the CAS framework (effective Aug'26). However, both are hurting less than the market feared. Prop traders have already found other funding, though at a higher cost. Volumes recovered by more than 20% in Sep'26, following the Aug'26 dip. The consultation paper also signals that CAS will be modified soon. We believe Groww should be a key beneficiary as volumes recover. A sideways market may continue to affect volumes in the near term. However, Groww is building new revenue streams in broking and beyond, which reduces its dependence on derivatives.
* Commodities offer a long runway for growth as penetration remains low. While Groww’s commodities business has grown strongly since launch, penetration among its active derivatives traders remains below the industry average. We expect growth to outpace the industry as awareness and adoption increase.
* MTF presents a significant opportunity to expand market share and improve cash-segment realizations. Groww’s MTF book has reached INR37.8b in 1Q, but its market share of less than 3% remains well below its 15% share of the cash segment. Its strong balance sheet provides ample capacity to scale the book and narrow this gap over time. As MTF trades are charged on an ad valorem basis, higher MTF activity can also improve cash-segment realizations.
* Lending, wealth management, and AMC are the next growth engines. These businesses are at different stages of build-out. Groww has a proven record of launching products at little extra cost, so each should add to profitability. The company has also not yet used its balance sheet to drive growth, which leaves a large lever untouched.
* Operating leverage multiplies earnings. In 1QFY27, Cost-to-Serve/Cost-to-Grow/ Cost-to-Operate dipped to 10.7%/9.9%/11.5% of platform revenue, from 14.6%/ 11.9%/18.3%. These improvements drove 101% YoY EBITDA growth and 94% YoY PAT growth. As customers use more products, each extra rupee of revenue should convert at higher margins.
* We expect Groww’s revenue/EBITDA/PAT to clock a CAGR of 31%/37%/38% over FY26-28. Our one-year TP is INR240, implying 38x FY28E EPS. Reiterate BUY.
 Broking: Regulatory normalization and deeper customer monetization support growth 
* Groww added 154k net active clients on the NSE in Sep’26 on a YoY basis, outpacing the industry’s net addition of 105k clients over the same period, taking transacting users to 23.5m (+24% YoY) as of Sep’26. Stock ADTO market share rose 3.3pp YoY to 15.1%, while retail equity-derivative market share increased to 11% from 7.2%.
* F&O contribution to total income declined to 52% in 1QFY27 from 56.4% in 1QFY26, offset by increasing contributions from MTF and commodities. We expect broking revenue to grow at 22% CAGR over FY26-28E, led by higher customer engagement and product penetration.
 * Stocks: Deeper monetization of existing users
** Retail stock ADTO market share increased to 15.1% (+3.3pp YoY), despite a sequential moderation following tighter risk controls. Stock ADTO grew 48% YoY, indicating sustained share gains.
** With 22m transacting users and INR3.6t of customer assets, MTF penetration remains the key lever to improve cash-segment realizations. We expect the stock-segment revenue to record 25% CAGR over FY26-28, supported by 10% order CAGR, active-user additions, and higher product attachment.
 ** Key monitorables: cash-equity market share, order growth, active users, and revenue per customer.
* Equity derivatives: Volume recovery remains the key near-term driver
** Retail equity derivatives maintained the market share at 11% in 2QFY27 (on a QoQ basis) vs. single-digit last year. We expect segment revenue to clock 16% CAGR over FY26-28, driven by market-share gains and gradual normalization in trading activity.
** CAS implementation on 3 rd Aug’26 triggered heightened volatility, particularly on expiry days, with F&O/cash ADTO declining 16%/2% MoM in Aug'26. Following SEBI's notification to partially reverse CAS implementation, F&O/cash ADTO recovered 20%/4% MoM in Sep'26.
 ** Key monitorables: F&O volumes, market share, regulatory changes, and expiryday activity.
 * Commodities: Low penetration supports outsized growth
** Commodity derivatives reached 435k active users in 1QFY27 (+10.7% QoQ), with a 2.6% attach rate to overall active users. Retail notional ADTO market share across MCX and NSE stood at 28.6%, indicating rapid share capture since launch.
** Penetration remains below the industry average among Groww's active derivative traders, providing headroom for further adoption. We expect the commodity-segment revenue and orders to register 110% CAGR over FY26- 28E, albeit on a low base.
 ** Key monitorables: active users, attach rate, ADTO market share, and revenue contribution.

docs.title: Buy HCL Technologies Ltd for the Target Rs 1,450 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
AI momentum strengthens, but guidance remains cautious Organic growth guidance unchanged at the midpoint; large-deal ramp-up to support FY28E growth 
* HCL Technologies (HCLT) reported 2QFY27 revenue of USD3.7b, rising 2.3% QoQ CC, below our estimate of 3% QoQ CC. EBIT margin came in at 18.2%, in line with our estimate of 18.1%. New deal TCV was USD3.3b (up 26.8% YoY) in 2QFY27. For FY27, revenue growth guidance was raised at the lower end to 2.5–4.0% YoY in CC (from 1.0-4.0%), driven by M&A; organic guidance remained unchanged. IT Services revenue growth guidance was revised to 3–4% YoY CC from 1.5–4.5%, reflecting a cut of 50bp at the upper end. EBIT margin guidance of 17.5–18.5% is in line with our estimates.
* For 1HFY27, revenue/EBIT/adj. PAT grew 12.7%/17.2%/20.8% YoY in INR terms. We expect revenue/EBIT/PAT to grow 9.1%/9.4%/11.2% YoY in 2HFY27. Free cash flow stood at 87% of net profit for 2QFY27. We reiterate our BUY rating with an unchanged TP of INR1,450, based on 18x FY28E EPS. We maintain HCLT as our preferred pick in the large cap space.
 Our view: Pipeline and bookings support near-term growth outlook, although macro uncertainty remains 
* FY27 organic growth guidance remains broadly unchanged at the midpoint, although the upper end has been lowered by 50bp. While we believe the market was not factoring in growth at the upper end, the reduction is a slight dampener. Services growth is expected to be better than the midpoint. The USD1.14b Mercedes-Benz deal is expected to start contributing in 1QFY28. We estimate ~1.3% contribution to growth and build in 5.1% YoY CC growth for FY28 versus 3.3% for FY27, with large-deal ramp-ups supporting growth into FY28.
* Advanced AI revenue grew 28.4% QoQ CC and 78% YoY CC to USD219m, equivalent to ~5.9% of quarterly revenue, with an annualized run rate of USD876m. Higher-margin AI services contributed 32bp to sequential EBIT margin expansion, while management indicated that Advanced AI services margins are expected to be 7–10pp above traditional services. Non-AI revenue remained subdued, declining 1% YoY.
* The Anthropic partnership expands HCLT’s enterprise AI ecosystem and monetization opportunities. The global premier partnership with Anthropic complements the existing Open AI relationship and is expected to support enterprise adoption of agentic AI, with a focus on safety, cybersecurity, and governance. Management indicated that implementation revenue will largely follow a services model, while integration of AI Force and other software products could support a more non-linear model, including token-related pricing.
* 1HFY27 bookings were the strongest ever for a first half, with 2Q bookings of USD3.3b, rising 27% YoY. Demand remained healthy toward the end of the quarter, although discretionary spending and the broader operating environment remain fluid. We expect large-deal ramp-ups and AI-led engagements to support sequential growth over the next 3–4 quarters.
* EBIT margin expanded 131bp QoQ to 18.2%, aided by operating efficiencies, operating leverage, and the contribution from Advanced AI. Management indicated that the desired margin band remains 18–19% but has not committed to a higher range, given the need to reinvest in capabilities and AI talent. We expect EBIT margin to reach 18% in FY28, with further expansion dependent on the balance between AI-led productivity gains and reinvestment.

* Wind capacity additions on track to meet FY27 targets: India added ~3GW of wind capacity in 1HFY27. Historically, as 2H installations have been 1.5x those in 1H, the implied addition of ~4.5GW in 2HFY27 would take FY27 additions to ~7.5GW, in line with the MNRE’s expectation of 7.5-8.0GW.
* Evening peak demand strengthens the case for wind: Rising power demand, particularly during evening peak hours, should support greater deployment of wind capacity through wind-solar hybrid and FDRE projects. As highlighted in the EAC-PM paper (Jul’26), average May evening peak prices rose from INR8.08/kWh in 2023 to INR9.40 in 2025 and INR9.71 in 2026. We believe strong merchant power prices in late evening reinforce the economic case for wind capacity.
 Execution-led growth with new opportunities
