ICICIAMC delivered steady performance in 2QFY27, with MF QAAUM growing ~4% qoq to Rs11.6trn, while revenue yields improved to 57.5bps, driving ~7% sequential revenue growth. EBITDA margin improved 20bps sequentially to 72.6% and was higher than our estimate, led by better-than-expected revenue growth. PAT at Rs8.89bn declined ~8% sequentially owing to lower other income given negative MTM movements but was ~4% higher than our estimate. The management mentioned that while the company saw some redemption pressure given market volatility, gross flows remained largely steady. MF revenue yields improved during the quarter, led by multiple factors, while alternate yields improved qoq, led by a change in the mix of alternate AUM. The management mentioned that it sees opportunities in the small-cap space and will gradually open up the mid-cap segment at an appropriate time. Baking in the 2Q developments, we tweak our estimates marginally, resulting in largely unchanged PAT over FY27-29E. We maintain BUY and Sep-27E TP of Rs3,800, implying FY28E PER of ~43x
 Steady quarter; yield improvement drives higher revenue 
During 2QFY27, AUM at Rs11.6trn grew ~4% qoq, while maintaining the second-highest market share of 13.3%. Revenue yields at 57.5bps improved qoq vs 56.3bps in 1QFY27, led by improvement in MF and alternate yields, driving revenue to Rs16.74bn (+7% qoq) and beating our estimate by ~3%. Other income dipped significantly to Rs169mn (from Rs1.8bn in 1QFY27). Employee cost at Rs2.12bn grew 4% sequentially during 2QFY27, while other expenses at Rs1.13bn grew 9% qoq. As a result, EBITDA at Rs12.15bn rose 7% qoq, largely owing to healthy revenue growth. EBITDA margin stood at 72.6% and was ahead of our estimate of 72.4%. PAT at Rs8.89bn increased 6% yoy and dipped 8% sequentially, driven by lower investment income, beating our estimate by 4%.
 Gross sales stable; addressing mid/small-cap gaps a long-term effort 
The management mentioned that the company saw redemption pressure in certain schemes, including hybrid schemes, while gross sales was largely steady. The management acknowledged that the company has not built a large franchise in the midand small-cap categories, given its positioning as a conservative AMC with higher share of hybrid funds. Ahead, the management sees building the mid- and small-cap segment as a 5-7-year effort. Further, it is currently pushing large-cap funds on better risk-reward and has opened up the small-cap category given the opportunity. The management mentioned that the company would look to gradually open up the mid-cap space as well, at an appropriate time. On the alternates side, in real estate funds, pre-leased office yield funds fit the company’s risk framework, and it plans to scale this category.
 We maintain BUY and Sep-27E TP of Rs3,800 
To bake in the 2Q developments, we tweak our estimates, resulting in largely unchanged PAT over FY27-29E. Led by its strong brand and distribution, ICICIAMC is poised to drive profitable AUM growth. We maintain BUY and Sep-27E TP of Rs3,800, implying FY28E PER of 43x.

RBL carries surplus liquidity, which it plans to deploy into wholesale and secured retail lending. Margins are expected to moderate in 3QFY27 due to the full-quarter impact of FCNR(B)-led leverage and surplus funds parked in lower-yielding assets, and partly offset by repo rate hike benefits, before recovering gradually in 4QFY27. Asset quality continued to improve, with gross slippages at 2.5% of loans, albeit still elevated. So far, the management has not seen any stress from the rural business or the Middle East conflict, although it remains watchful. However, the management expects card slippages to stabilize at ~Rs4bn in 3Q/4QFY27. We tweak our earnings estimates and retain BUY on RBL, while raising TP by 10.5% to Rs475 from Rs430 (roll forward to 1.6x Sep-28E ABV).
 Credit growth accelerates; margin recovery likely in 4QFY27 
Credit growth accelerated to ~42% yoy/~22% qoq, driven by broad-based growth across segments along with FCNR B leverage, while the cards portfolio remained muted. The bank continues to hold surplus liquidity, which was partly utilized to retire high-cost borrowings and bulk TDs, with the rest deployed in short-term investments and wholesale loans. Going forward, the bank plans to deploy this liquidity into wholesale lending and secured retail expansion. Management expects credit card balances to stabilize in the coming quarter and retrace positive growth over the next 6M. Margins are likely to decline modestly next quarter due to the full-quarter impact of FCNR(B)-led leverage and surplus liquidity parked in lower-yielding assets, partly offset by repo rate hike benefits before likely gradually recovering in 4Q as funds are deployed into advances

However, slippages for cards has improved (though still elevated), while MFI slippages increased qoq. Further, Management indicated Retail collections, including rural businesses, were stable, with no material impact from the Middle East conflict so far. Management expects card slippages to stabilize at ~Rs4bn in 3Q/4QFY27, with credit costs declining to ~6% from a low double-digit level.
 We retain BUY on RBL; raise TP by 10.5% to Rs475 
We tweak our earnings estimates and expect the bank to deliver a gradual improvement in ROA to 1-1.3% over FY27-29E. We retain BUY, while revising up our TP by 10.5% to Rs475 from Rs430, based on 1.6x Sep-28E ABV. Key risks: Delay in asset quality recovery in MFI/cards, slower business growth, and KMP attrition.

docs.title: Buy Piramal Finance Ltd for the Target Rs 2,480 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Growth in the kitty; profitability is next 
etail transformation behind us; a richer product mix and operating leverage to drive a sharper RoA-led earnings upcycle
 * Growth engine firing; multiple avenues support ~25% AUM CAGR: Piramal Finance has moved decisively beyond its balance-sheet transition phase. Growth AUM now accounts for ~98% of the portfolio, while retail contributes ~85% of AUM, leaving the legacy book at less than 2%. With retail disbursements rising ~44% YoY to INR125b in 1QFY27 and consolidated AUM rising ~25% YoY, visibility on the company’s ~25% FY27 AUM growth target remains strong. Importantly, growth is becoming more diversified. The established housing and LAP franchise is being complemented by gold loans, MFI, micro-LAP, unsecured lending and deeper cross-sell to its ~6m customer base. Cross-sell already contributes ~28-29% of business volumes, creating an opportunity to grow the franchise with lower customer-acquisition costs and potentially better credit outcomes.
 * The next earnings lever will be richer portfolio mix and lower cost of funds: We see increasing scope for margin expansion as incremental originations are skewed toward higher-yielding, shorter-tenure businesses. Gold loans, MFI, micro-LAP and unsecured lending carry higher disbursement yields than the existing portfolio, and as these books season, the richer origination mix should progressively lift portfolio yields. At the same time, Piramal's improving credit ratings and greater access to diversified and multilateral funding should support a gradual reduction in cost of borrowings. Thus, we believe the next leg of NIM expansion is increasingly structural rather than purely rate-cycle driven. We estimate NIM at ~5.4%/5.9% in FY27E/FY28E.
 * Operating leverage is emerging as the biggest profitability catalyst: The strongest change in the earnings profile is the widening gap between business growth and cost growth. In 1QFY27, AUM grew ~25% YoY, while opex increased only ~10%, driving the cost-to-income ratio down sharply to ~52.5% from 65.6% a year earlier. The Opex/AUM ratio has dipped consistently over the past eight quarters to 3.5% from 4.9%, despite the resumption of branch expansion. Technology and AI should further reinforce this operating leverage by allowing Piramal to scale underwriting, collections and operations without a commensurate increase in costs. Management expects opex/AUM to dip another ~40- 50bp over the next 4-5 quarters and is targeting ~2.5% RoAUM by 4QFY27.
 * From growth to earnings – Piramal Finance is transitioning from the hard-work phase to the payoff phase: With the legacy book largely behind it, we believe the company has reached an important inflection point. We expect the convergence of ~25% AUM CAGR, improving NIMs, operating leverage and controlled credit costs to drive a sharp earnings recovery. We estimate PAT CAGR of ~55% over FY26-28E, with RoA/RoE improving to 2.8%/11.4% by FY28E.
* The ~INR38.5b primary equity infusion further strengthens the capital base, providing greater flexibility to pursue disciplined growth while maintaining a prudent risk profile. The stock currently trades at ~1.3x FY28E P/BV. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR2,480, based on our Mar'28E SoTP valuation.
* Piramal Finance is entering a phase where the benefits of its multi-year transformation can increasingly translate into earnings. With the legacy book largely behind it, a scalable retail franchise, a richer business mix, lower funding costs, improving operating leverage and disciplined credit outcomes provide a stronger foundation for sustained profitability improvement.
* The ~INR38.5b capital infusion further strengthens its balance sheet flexibility to fund growth while maintaining a prudent capital buffer. With Piramal Finance targeting ~2.5% RoAUM by 4QFY27 and >3% over the longer term, the improving operating architecture provides a credible pathway to sustained earnings expansion.
* We model a total AUM CAGR of ~25% and PAT CAGR of ~55% over FY26- FY28E, with RoA/RoE reaching 2.8%/11% by FY28E. We reiterate our BUY rating with a TP of INR 2,480 (based on our Mar’28E SoTP).
